📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erielle Sudario is a Collider News and Feature Author from Australia and has worked in the journalism industry since 2018. She has a passion for entertainment and pop culture news and has interviewed YouTubers, voice actors, film directors, and musicians throughout her career. When she's not writing, you can see Erielle building keyboards, reading a good book, playing video games, and creating content on social media.

Before Harry Potter entered theaters in 2001, a highly praised children's novel was adapted into a film. The feature had a star-studded cast and earned praise from fans and critics alike. 30 years later, the feature has captured a latest audience and become a streaming hit.

The film in question is Matilda, a children's fantasy movie based on Roald Dahl's book of the same name, starring Mara Wilson as Matilda, a young girl who discovers she has powers. Unlike Stephen King's Carrie, a horror story that also follows a young girl with powers, Matilda uses her newfound abilities to help others. The book came out in 1988, and the film adaptation, which also starred Danny DeVito (It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia), Rhea Perlman (Barbie), and Pam Ferris (Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban), was released in 1996.

Recent findings suggest that recently, Matilda became a streaming hit on HBO Max, landing at #4 on the platform's Top 10 Movies Worldwide, sitting between The End of Oak Street and The Legend of Tarzan. Since its release, Matilda has grossed $47 million worldwide and earned a Certified Fresh critics score of 90% and an audience score of 73% on Rotten Tomatoes, plus a 3.8-star rating on Letterboxd.

Sources indicate that four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

According to recent reports, you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Roald Dahl was a British author born in 1916 and died in 1990, known for his children's books. Matilda is one of many books in Dahl's collection adapted to screen. Another popular entry is Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, a 1964 book that received two film adaptations and a prequel. The first came out in 1971 as Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory and starred Gene Wilder as Willy Wonka. It was adapted again in 2005, starring Johnny Depp as Willy Wonka and Freddie Highmore as Charlie Bucket. Then, in 2023, a prequel to the 1971 feature was released, called Wonka, starring Timothée Chalamet as a young Willy Wonka who has yet to build his chocolate factory. In 1996, a film adaptation of James and the Giant Peach was released, based on Dahl's 1961 novel of the same name, but it was a box-office failure, earning only $28.9 million. There's also The BFG (Big Friendly Giant), a children's book that was first published in 1982. The book received two film adaptations. The first came out in 1989, and the second, directed by Steven Spielberg, came out in 2016 and earned nearly $200 million worldwide.

Matilda is available to stream on The Roku Channel. Follow Collider for more updates.

Yellowjackets Season 4 Features The Show's Most Heartbreaking Scene Yet

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spoilers ahead for "Yellowjackets" Season 4, Episode 1, "Hivemind.".
  • "Yellowjackets" Season 4 isn't letting up on the heartache, even now that the girls are out of the Wilderness.
  • Recent findings suggest that last season, Natalie snuck away from the girls' latest cannibal hunt and used a salvaged satellite phone to call for help.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for "Yellowjackets" Season 4, Episode 1, "Hivemind.".

"Yellowjackets" Season 4 isn't letting up on the heartache, even now that the girls are out of the Wilderness. The show has had plenty of tearjerking moments already, from Jackie's (Ella Purnell) death in Season 1 to Shauna's (Sophie Nélisse) stillbirth in Season 2. But "Hivemind" has one to rival all of those, especially if, like me, Natalie (Sophie Thatcher) is your favorite.

Recent findings suggest that last season, Natalie snuck away from the girls' latest cannibal hunt and used a salvaged satellite phone to call for help. "Hivemind" picks up with everyone freshly rescued and recuperating in a Canadian hospital. The team's parents all fly in — including the parents who then discover that their kids didn't make it, like Mari's (Alexa Barajas) mom (Patricia De León).

Industry observers note that the surviving Yellowjackets and their parents reunite — except for Natalie, because her mom didn't bother to show up. That everyone else's parents came only makes it worse, like the universe twisting the knife in her side yet again. She has to stand alone surrounded by reminders of the parental love she's never had and face that she's back to being the neglected kid she was before the plane crash. No wonder Natalie makes a quick exit and bums a cigarette off a hospital worker.

When Natalie hears the authorities couldn't reach her mother, she smiles through the tears and says "sounds about right." You spend 19 months thinking your daughter is probably dead, and you don't drop everything when there's a chance she isn't? What kind of mother does that? We've seen before that Natalie had a rough home life. Her dad was an abusive drunk, and when Natalie threatened him with a rifle, he grabbed it and accidentally shot himself, for which Natalie's mother blames her.

Recent findings suggest that when we initially see Natalie in "Hivemind," she's taking her first hot shower in 19 months, as if also washing off her brutal time in the Wilderness and her sins while there. Then the rest of the episode drops cold water on her. She kept her teammates alive through the winter as a hunter and leader, and she led the effort to get them home in the last stretch of Season 3. Her reward is resettling into her crappy life.

On one hand, it's easy to forget struggles like a broken home when you're stuck miles away from civilization. Or, alternatively, this only makes Natalie more heroic, for she knew she didn't have much of a home to go back to but still risked everything for everyone else. But let's not overlook Natalie's (cannibalistic) complicity, either. She's the team's savior but not a saint, and that conflict is what makes her so compelling.

Back in the Season 2 episode "It Chooses," Natalie — the starving girls' chosen sacrifice — lets Javi (Luciano Leroux) drown so they can eat him instead. I asked after Season 2 if we'd been misjudging Natalie as the "good one," the same question Natalie was asking herself. Now, I'd say the answer is yes and no. She's good but not so much that she'll throw her own life away for someone else. Most people never have their morality put to the test like that, but Natalie did. She failed and has to live with proof of the kind of person she is. Now, in "Hivemind," she faces what the life she fought to hold onto so hard looks like. Before she could assuage her guilt with the imagination of rescue, now the reality can't give her that same solace.

In a recent development, when Natalie goes for the smoke, the hospital worker says she shouldn't be smoking. "I shouldn't be alive," Natalie replies. Is she talking about the realistic odds of surviving 19 months stranded? Of trading her life for Javi's? Of deserving to be alive? All of the above? Searching for comfort with a cigarette ties together well with Natalie in the adult timeline (Juliette Lewis), who had developed a drug addiction to cope with her guilt.

Natalie also said in the pilot, during a rehab group session, that she lost her purpose after the Wilderness. Now we know that she had blossomed into a leader out there. It's important to contrast her with the group's other queens, Shauna and Lottie, because all three became people they couldn't be back home.

Sources indicate that lottie, without access to her medication, embraced her illness as clairvoyance and became a prophet. Shauna lived in Jackie's shadow her whole life, then came into her own in the most horrifying way possible. Before the plane crash, Natalie was viewed by everyone as a burnout. She was already hitting drugs and liquor in high school, and her teammates looked down on her for that, for her sexual proclivity, and for being poorer than them. In the Wilderness, she became a leader without intending to become one.

In "Hivemind," Lottie is almost catatonic, and Shauna is stewing in silent anger. None of the three Antler Queens are going to have an easy time readjusting, but with Natalie, it feels like she could have if she'd had a better support system waiting for her. Natalie's mom not showing up for her may lack the violence of other "Yellowjackets" tearjerker moments, but it remains quietly heartbreaking all the same.

"Yellowjackets" is streaming on Paramount+.

Claude vs. ChatGPT: 5 key differences that could change which AI you use

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1339 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that chatGPT and Claude are two of the biggest names in AI, and both have become significantly more capable within the last few months.
  • ChatGPT has evolved into an all-purpose assistant with tools for everything from image generation and voice conversations to coding and research.
  • I've spent plenty of time testing both, and while there's considerable overlap between what they can do, there are some differences worth understanding before deciding which one deserves your time and money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that chatGPT and Claude are two of the biggest names in AI, and both have become significantly more capable within the last few months. Whether you need help writing an email, researching a topic, creating an app or managing your workload, both chatbots can handle far more than simple questions and answers. But despite their similarities, OpenAI and Anthropic have taken different approaches to building their AI assistants.

ChatGPT has evolved into an all-purpose assistant with tools for everything from image generation and voice conversations to coding and research. Claude has become hyper-focused on writing, programming and helping users complete more complicated tasks through its growing collection of productivity tools.Now that Anthropic has gone public, people are beginning to wonder what is so special about the company's AI known as Claude.

I've spent plenty of time testing both, and while there's considerable overlap between what they can do, there are some differences worth understanding before deciding which one deserves your time and money.

Here are five of the biggest differences between Claude and ChatGPT.

In a recent development, claude has developed a reputation for producing natural-sounding text that is especially true for longer pieces. It's also good at following detailed writing instructions and maintaining a consistent tone and style across multiple rounds of editing.

Sources indicate that and while ChatGPT is no slouch when it comes to writing, either, it has the advantage of flexibility. You can ask it to rewrite something in five different tones, brainstorm headline ideas or transform a complicated explanation into something a beginner can understand.So, while Claude may be the better starting point for someone writing a novel or polishing a lengthy document, ChatGPT is especially useful when experimenting with different approaches.

Of course, writing quality is subjective. The results also depend on which model you're using and how clearly you explain what you want.

One of ChatGPT's biggest advantages is how many different types of tasks it can handle within the same experience.

Sources indicate that alongside traditional text conversations, ChatGPT supports image generation and editing. You can describe a picture you want to create, upload an existing image to change its appearance or use the chatbot to develop visual concepts.

ChatGPT also offers voice conversations, so customers can speak naturally with the assistant instead of typing everything into a chat window.

Claude has expanded its creative capabilities, too, particularly through Artifacts, which lets users create interactive content, visualizations and applications.

However, Claude's creative tools are more focused on building useful digital experiences than generating standalone images.

For anyone who regularly switches between writing, visual creation and spoken conversations, ChatGPT offers a more versatile experience.

Coding or "vibe coding" has become one of the biggest battlegrounds between Anthropic and OpenAI.

Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent, designed to work directly with codebases, understand existing projects, make changes and help developers solve complicated programming problems.

It has become particularly popular with developers who want an AI assistant that can work inside their existing development environment.

OpenAI's answer is Codex, which can also navigate repositories, write code, fix bugs and handle development tasks.

According to recent reports, both tools go well beyond generating snippets of code in a chatbot. They can take on larger assignments and work through multiple steps of a project.

The biggest difference is often how developers prefer to work. Claude Code has strong roots in terminal-based development, while Codex offers workflows across different development environments and agent-based tasks.

It has been revealed that for casual owners who occasionally need help building a website or debugging a script, either chatbot can be useful. Developers working on larger projects may find that their preferred coding agent becomes the deciding factor. Personally, I tend to hit my usage limits and blast through tokens faster with Claude Code,.

One of the most interesting changes to Claude is Anthropic's growing focus on turning the chatbot into a coworker.

With Cowork, Claude can take on more complicated assignments involving files, documents and connected tools. Rather than walking through every step in a conversation, owners can describe the outcome they want and let Claude work through the assignment.

For example, someone could ask Claude to organize project materials, work through a collection of documents or prepare files for a presentation.

ChatGPT is moving in a similar direction with its own agent capabilities, including ChatGPT Work and Codex.

The difference is how these experiences are organized and presented to owners. Anthropic has emphasized the idea of Claude as a digital coworker that can take responsibility for larger assignments. OpenAI has built a broader ecosystem that includes conversational assistance, research, creative tools and specialized agents.

Neither approach is inherently better, but if you're looking for an AI assistant to do more than answer questions, knowing the difference is notable.

Price is another consideration, particularly if you're not sure how often you'll use an AI chatbot.

Both companies offer free access, although usage limits and available features vary.

It has been revealed that chatGPT Plus and Claude Pro each cost $20 per month in the United States. ChatGPT also offers a lower-priced Go subscription for $8 per month, giving consumers another option between the free and Plus tiers.

Claude offers annual billing for Pro, which can reduce the effective monthly cost for owners willing to commit to a full year.

Of course, usage limits, access to more powerful models and included tools can make one subscription more valuable than another. For example, if you think you're going to be creating more images and want that type of creativity from a model, than you'll want to go with ChatGPT. At the same time, if you're a casual user looking for an affordable upgrade, ChatGPT offers more flexibility in its pricing. But, if you rely heavily on Claude's writing and coding capabilities, Pro may be worth the investment.

Recent findings suggest that here's some good news: you don't have to choose between one or the other. Because ChatGPT offers so much for free, it might be worth sticking with it. But, if you find yourself going through tokens much faster with Claude, you might want to consider bumping up your subscription to a paid tier. I use both agents for different things, which brings me to another point. The bigger question is what you want your AI assistant to do.

Claude is particularly appealing for people who spend their days writing, coding or working through complicated projects. Its emphasis on natural language and increasingly capable agent tools makes it a strong choice for serious productivity work.

Sources indicate that chatGPT offers a broader experience. Between image generation, voice conversations, research, coding and its growing collection of productivity features, it's designed to serve as an assistant for almost anything.

If you want one AI chatbot that can handle the widest variety of everyday tasks, start with ChatGPT. If your priorities are writing, coding and managing complex workflows, Claude deserves a serious look. And since both offer free versions, the easiest way to decide is to give them the same five prompts and see which one delivers the results you actually prefer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don't read any poems about ravens if you haven't seen "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Spoilers ahead!

It has been revealed that we don't know precisely when the Hunger Games world exists. We just know, from the books and films, that North America has been redrawn into a totalitarian regime called Panem by that point in the future. There's a very interesting reference to American culture, though, in both the novel and movie version of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," the origin story of future District 12 mentor and rebel Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada in this film). Specifically, Edgar Allan Poe's poem "The Raven" just ... exists.

Recent findings suggest that the book takes great pains to "transform" this poem — which begins with the line "Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary" — into a song, which gives Haymitch's girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak) her first name. As Haymitch notes of Lenore Dove, a member of District 12's musical Covey, "She tends to take a dark view of things, but maybe that's to be expected from someone named for a dead girl. Well, half for the dead girl called Lenore in this old poem and half for a shade of gray, which I found out the day I met her.".

In case you're foggy on "The Raven," here's a snippet:.

Ah, distinctly I remember it was in the bleak December; And each separate dying ember wrought its ghost upon the floor. Eagerly I wished the morrow;—vainly I had sought to borrow From my books surcease of sorrow—sorrow for the lost Lenore— For the rare and radiant maiden whom the angels name Lenore— Nameless here for evermore.

Industry observers note that interestingly, the "Sunrise on the Reaping" book by Suzanne Collins never mentions Poe by name. The movie, however, takes a different approach.

It has been revealed that again, in Suzanne Collins' 2025 novel "Sunrise on the Reaping," the author makes it clear that "The Raven" is a song of, I suppose, unknown provenance. As Haymitch explains while he's preparing for the Games, he keeps dreaming about Lenore and thinking about what he calls her "name song," saying, "In it, a guy loses the love of his life, Lenore, and he's going crazy for missing her. Then this big old raven reveals up at his house and won't leave and whenever he asks the bird anything, it just says 'Nevermore' — which, as you can imagine, just makes him crazier.".

Across the board, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is a pretty faithful adaptation of the novel, and a scene between Haymitch and Capitol cameraman Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons on-screen) plays out roughly the same as it does on the page. There is one notable difference, though, which is that the film has a physical prop book that says "'The Raven' by Edgar Allan Poe" on the cover.

Industry observers note that both versions have Plutarch ask Haymitch if he knows what "nepenthe," a mythical potion, means when the Hunger Games tribute sees a bottle of it on a bar. When Plutarch inquires if Haymitch has heard of it in the book, he internally scoffs: "Not only have I heard of it, I know it from the poem that gave my love her name. I'm tired of being patronized, so I decide to put him in his place." When Haymitch recites a line about nepenthe from the poem, Plutarch finishes it in both versions. So, why is this poem so horrifyingly perfect for this Hunger Games story?

Putting aside the wild idea of Edgar Allan Poe being, I think, the only tangible link between our world and Panem, Suzanne Collins picked a horribly appropriate name for Lenore Dove Baird. The woman in "The Raven" is, obviously, dead, and by the end of "Sunrise on the Reaping," Lenore Dove meets the same fate.

When Haymitch, working with fellow tribute Ampert Latier (Percy Daggs IV) and Ampert's father, Haymitch's assigned mentor, and former District 3 victor Beetee (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), tries to destroy the Games arena itself by blowing up a subterranean water tank, he does technically succeed. Unfortunately, the water tank bursts, yet the arena remains intact, and Haymitch wins the Games by utilizing a force field just outside of the arena's range ... and is summarily punished when he returns home to District 12. Not only does he find his house burning to ash immediately upon arrival, he learns that his mother and younger brother, his only family members, are inside. Then, not long after, he reunites with Lenore and feeds her a gumdrop, her favorite candy ... but it's a poisoned bag direct from President Snow, and she dies, too.

It has been revealed that "The raven. The unforgiving songbird. Repeatedly reminding me of President Snow's crystal-clear message to me on my homecoming," Haymitch thinks to himself bitterly as he mourns. "That I will never get to love anyone ever again. Nevermore. Because he will make sure they end up dying a horrible death." Still, the word "Nevermore" ends the film adaptation as Haymitch surveys the now-peaceful reaping site, giving it a slightly brighter meaning when the story ends on-screen.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

She also expressed real regret for having made the statement at all. In a recent apology statement, she said:.

To be honest, I’m embarrassed. I’m genuinely embarrassed that I noted that. I don’t remember the intention behind it because I know I wasn’t trying to get into a street fight, like a physical fight. It’s genuinely embarrassing. I don’t know why the hell I said that.

Anytime you get a group of people together who come from different backgrounds, have them spend long periods of time together, and point cameras at them, you’re bound to get some drama as they get to know each other. It was a bit unusual that this particular drama came from someone not actually in the room where it happened, but it sounds like Mayci has definitely learned a lesson from the fallout. She went on to say:.

I am very sorry I mentioned that. I did regret saying that. That is definitely out of character for me. … I’m just going to be accountable for the things that I was upset with myself for. I’ve apologized for it, and moving on.

After the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody complications with her children, and her declared departure, it immediately turned attention to the new spinoff and the drama in the OC. So, I’m glad that Mayci didn’t seem to waste any time in sharing such an honest reaction to her own behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are a lot of characters in the wider "Hunger Games" universe, so I'll forgive you if you're only familiar with some of the bigger players like Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada in his origin film and Woody Harrelson in the original movies), Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth, Ralph Fiennes, and Donald Sutherland at various points throughout his life), Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), or Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler). The latest installment in the literary and cinematic franchise, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," brings back some familiar faces and introduces new ones too — so, who, exactly, is Proserpina Trinket?

Recent findings suggest that introduced in both the book and film version of "Sunrise on the Reaping," Proserpina Trinket is a bubbly, enthusiastic, and quick-thinking young stylist working to prepare Hunger Games tributes for all the Capitol-centric pomp and circumstance that takes place before the bloody Games themselves. (Yes, the teenage tributes get all dolled up before they're forced to fight to the death in a dangerous arena that's also trying to kill them. This world is sick!).

Recent findings suggest that we don't know a ton about Prosperina besides the fact that she works with the extremely unreliable Magno Stift (Billy Porter), she's assigned to work on Zada's Haymitch alongside Vitus (Edvin Ryding), and her older sister is future District 12 chaperone and stylist Effie Trinket (played in this film by Elle Fanning and the original movies by Elizabeth Banks). What we definitely know is that she's played by Iris Apatow, a rising talent from a famous family who's shown up in a handful of TV reveals and several huge comedy movies from the 2000s.

Iris Apatow was born in 2002, and odds are you're familiar with her family. Her older sister, Maude Apatow, starred in "Euphoria" throughout its entire run. Her mother, Leslie Mann, is an acclaimed comedic actor. Then there's her dad Judd Apatow, a comedy kingmaker, producer, writer, and director who's helped make projects like "Superbad" and "Bridesmaids" and directed his own like "The 40-Year-Old Virgin," "Knocked Up," "Funny People," and "This is 40." Let's talk about those last three, because all of them feature the youngest Apatow. (The less mentioned about Judd Apatow's 2022 COVID movie "The Bubble," the better.).

Industry observers note that maude and Iris Apatow play Sadie and Charlotte, respectively, in both "Knocked Up" and "This is 40" — with their on-screen mother, Debbie, portrayed by Mann, and their father Pete by Paul Rudd as an Apatow stand-in. As for "Funny People," they also play Mann's daughters (in this one, Maude is Mable and Iris is Ingrid) with Mann as Laura, the ex-girlfriend of comedian and actor George Simmons (Adam Sandler), who's dealing with a life-changing health crisis. Sure, the Apatow daughters don't do a ton here, but they flesh out the universe in all three of their dad's films ... and it's notable that we watched Maude and Iris grow up on-screen, basically.

Industry observers note that all things considered, Iris Apatow's career is just getting started. Still, over the past few years, she's dabbled in more adult fare (especially on the small screen), so it definitely seems like she's trying to show off her range.

According to recent reports, from 2016 to 2018, Apatow portrayed a supporting character, Arya Hopkins, who's tutored by series lead Gus (Paul Rust) on the Netflix TV show "Love," while on another Netflix exclusive, "Unstable," she appeared alongside Rob Lowe and his real-life son John Owen Love. The latter duo play tech CEO Ellis Dragon and his creatively inclined son Jackson, respectively, whereas Apatow plays Anna, an intern at Ellis' organization, itself aptly named Dragon, who also happens to be the former stepdaughter of the company's CFO Anna ("Fleabag" standout Sian Clifford).

Sources indicate that then there's "Tell Me Lies." A deliciously dramatic and dishy Hulu series created by Meaghan Oppenheimer, "Tell Me Lies" adapts (and improves) the book of the same name by Carola Lovering and ran for three seasons on Hulu. Apatow shows up as a college student named Amanda in the third and final season, creating a problem for series regular Bree (Cat Missal) as she mentally and emotionally recovers from an affair with a professor named Oliver (Tom Ellis). After she finally gets out of Oliver's clutches, Bree notices that Amanda seems to be Oliver's next victim, sending her into a spiral.

You can see Apatow as Proserpina in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Happy weekend! The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is out in theaters, seemingly putting an end to one of the biggest franchises in recent years. It’s pretty good.

If you prefer to stay home, you have plenty of options. Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is out on VOD and finally available to watch on your TV. The movie stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, following him and his crew of men as they try to return home in the aftermath of the devastating Trojan War.

According to recent reports, other major releases include Steps, Netflix’s latest animated movie, following Cinderella’s evil stepsisters, with one of them forced to team up with her in order to save their realm. It’s voiced by Amanda Seyfried, Ali Wong, Stephanie Tsu, Daniel Radcliffe, and more.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for horror or drama with a healthy dose of disturbing material, Netflix has two options: Insidious: Out of the Further follows a mom plagued by awful nightmares that might be missives from a parallel dimension; Gentle Monster follows a pianist and a mother who moves to the country with her family looking for a break from city life. Then her husband is accused by the police of serious crimes.

According to recent reports, other horror movies are available on VOD. There’s The Ice Cream Man, following an ice cream seller whose frozen desserts turn kids into killers, and Appofeniacs, a series of horror snippets exploring AI.

Industry observers note that other highlights include Nicolas Cage's Best Pancakes in the County, the Anthony Bourdain biopic Tony, and the Patricia Highsmith-inspired psychological thriller A Talent for Murder. There’s also The Beast, a newly introduced Samuel L. Jackson film where he stars as a President trying to survive a terrorist attack with only a wounded Secret Service Agent for protection. Happy watching.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps the biggest film of the year is finally available on streaming. Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey adapts the story of Odysseus (Matt Damon) to the screen in appropriately epic fashion and format, having him face giants, witches, sea monsters, mermaids, and much more as he tries to return home to his wife (Anne Hathaway) and son (Tom Holland).

It has been revealed that the Odyssey opens with a gentle warning: "A time of apparent magic," a gentle prod at audiences to both accept and question what they're about to see. Yet Ithaca, and the Palace of Odysseus, is all too devoid of magic. His wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) has spent the last 20 years waiting for her husband (Matt Damon) to return home from the Trojan War, while a small army of suitors vies to replace him. Running out of time before lead suitor Antinous (Robert Pattinson) can seal the deal, Odysseus' son Telemachus (Tom Holland) sets out on a journey to either find his dad or prove he's dead and claim the crown (either option seems fine for the young lad).

Sources indicate that netflix’s latest animated film takes the well-trodden story of Cinderella and reinvents it through a fresh perspective. It tells the story from the side of her evil stepsisters. The story follows Lilith (Ali Wong), who accidentally turns her sister Margot (Stephanie Tsu) into a frog. To bring her sister back, she has to team up with her estranged stepsister Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried) to save the kingdom.

In a recent development, the star-studded cast of Steps works hard to give depth to characters who, for all intents and purposes, were completely shallow in their original tales. Wong is known for her sharpness and her comedy. She meshes well with this more modern take on the ugly stepsister, but she’s just as capable of hitting you where it hurts when the story calls for it. Her anger at being unaccepted and belittled by the people around her, while Cinderella only has to exist to be loved, is heartbreaking to watch.

In a recent development, insidious: Out of the Further is finally out on Netflix. The film expands on the successful Blumhouse franchise, focusing on a different family. It follows Gemma (Amelia Eve), a single mother traumatized by a childhood dominated by an absent mother and a terrifying incident. As she begins to have strange dreams, she starts to scare her daughter and mirror her mother’s erratic behavior.

In a recent development, written and directed by Mary Kreutzer, Gentle Monster follows a concert pianist (Lea Seydoux) who relocates to the countryside after her husband claims burnout. As the film progresses, we learn that her husband is facing some serious accusations from the police.

It has been revealed that based on a pivotal summer in Anthony Bourdain’s life, Tony is set in 1975, following a 19-year-old fictional version of Bourdain who relocates to Provincetown to follow his high school crush. After a series of slips and disasters, he ends up getting a job as a dishwasher in a restaurant.

Sources indicate that nicolas Cage stars in this thriller, which has drawn comparisons to Tarantino, playing a criminal on the run from a botched heist. He hides in a diner, triggering a face-off with all sorts of enemies, including federal agents, criminals, and more, putting a seemingly innocent waitress and line cook at risk.

Eli Roth’s latest film follows a strange and mysterious ice cream man (Ari Millen) who serves frozen desserts that turn kids into violent killers.

Set in 1995, A Talent for Murder follows an editor from New York (Alden Ehrenreich) who’s been sent to the Swiss Alps to convince Patricia Highsmith (Helen Mirren) to write a new Tom Ripley novel. There, she challenges him to help her craft the perfect murder.

According to recent reports, appofeniacs contains various stories, all centered on the impact of AI. It follows a troll wreaking chaos on people’s lives by creating AI deepfakes, including a smear campaign, putting a man's life and career at risk, and more.

The Beast is an action-thriller starring Samuel L. Jackson. The premise is wild: the US President (Jackson), a former U.S. veteran, gets stranded at an international summit, with his protective detail wiped out in an attack. He’s left alone with a wounded Secret Service agent (Joel Kinnaman) as the two try to survive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: This article contains SPOILERS for Agatha All Along.

Industry observers note that agatha All Along's central witch coven comprises seven different characters, each with their own specialties, powers, stories, and Marvel connections. Agatha All Along's MCU story stems from the climactic ending of WandaVision. The latter show centered on the Scarlet Witch and her inadvertent enslavement of the town of Westview. The villain of the show was Agatha herself, played by Kathryn Hahn once more in Agatha All Along's cast of characters.

Sources indicate that given that WandaVision is one of the better-ranked MCU shows thus far, Agatha All Along was highly anticipated, especially considering the former show's creator and writer, Jac Schaeffer, possesses the same roles in the latter. What makes Agatha All Along's MCU story even more interesting, however, is the show's new batch of characters.

The series is a fun, spooky, Halloween-inspired MCU show centering on witches from across the MCU, meaning each character has their own intriguing stories, power sets, connections to Agatha, and links to Marvel Comics.

Industry observers note that beginning with the titular character, Agatha Harkness is a former witch from Salem, Massachusetts. Agatha belonged to her own coven long ago but was accused of practicing dark magic during the Salem witch trials. After her coven attempted to cast her out, Agatha's dark magic attacked her peers, including her mother, killing them and setting Agatha down a path of villainy and evil. 300 years later, Agatha was drawn to Westview after Wanda Maximoff covered the town in a witch hex, with the former seeking to harness the latter's chaos magic.

Agatha failed to draw Wanda's power from her and had her own drained in the process, leading the latter to enslave the former in Westview seemingly permanently. In Agatha All Along, the titular witch is freed from her prison and embarks on a quest down the Witches Road. At the end of it, Agatha hopes to recover what will make her whole again: her powers.

Industry observers note that in the comics, Agatha's origins are similar to those from WandaVision. Agatha was involved in the Salem Witch Trials in the comics, only with the difference that she orchestrated them to cull the weak from her coven. Over the centuries, Agatha spends a lot of time trying to build her power in multiple covens, training several magic users, and even fighting in wars like the American Revolutionary War and defeating Nazi sorcerers during World War II.

Sources indicate that eventually, Agatha crossed paths with The Fantastic Four when she became the governess of Franklin Richards, often aiding the team and even teaching Franklin to hone his powers. Through The Fantastic Four, she met Wanda Maximoff. Agatha became the mentor to Wanda and other magic customers in the modern Marvel Comics era and has been killed and subsequently resurrected multiple times. In the current continuity, Agatha is alive, though is rarely seen in stories.

In a recent development, like the other strong sorcerers of the Marvel universe, Agatha's powers are a gateway to almost endless abilities. From energy and elemental manipulation and binding spells to dimensional manipulation, flight, force fields, and illusions, Agatha is one of the most powerful magic users in the Marvel Comics pantheon. This is without mentioning her telepathy, telekinesis, and the tens of other abilities she possesses through her magical training.

Recent findings suggest that while Agatha's powers are gone in Agatha All Along as a result of Wanda's spell on the witch at the end of WandaVision, it appears Harkness still believes she has the ability to absorb the powers of other magic-customers if they direct their abilities at her. However, it's unclear whether this is indeed true, or rather the character's own hopes as she attempts everything to retrieve her former abilities once more.

According to recent reports, one of the other witches who joins Agatha and Teen down the Witches Road is Lilia Calderu, played by Patti LuPone. In the context of Agatha’s coven, Calderu serves as an expert in divination. Divination is the practice of seeking knowledge about the future via supernatural means. In Calderu’s case in Agatha All Along, she suffers from various visions and flashes of foresight, making her seem somewhat more unhinged than the witches around her.

Because of her powers, Lilia is shown to be aware of some of the details of Agatha's past, telling the witch that she knows Agatha has been under the influence of "someone you hurt" and who then took her agency for 3 years. This - combined with Lilia's own experience of witch history, since Agatha suggests she's 450 years old - it's likely Lilia could provide more insight about Agatha's backstory as the show continues, since she's clearly able to access information that the witch may otherwise not be willing to reveal.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Hexed" is right now eyeing an opening in the $23 million range, per Box Office Theory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that disney has produced many of the best animated movies of all time. They've been doing it longer than anyone else and, arguably, better than anyone else for decades. Unfortunately though, original animation has been a tough sell to audiences in recent years, and Disney's "Hexed" looks like it's going to suffer at the box office as a result of this trend.

"Hexed" is right now eyeing an opening in the $23 million range, per Box Office Theory. That's across the full five-day, Wednesday to Sunday stretch since this movie is opening mid-week for the Thanksgiving holiday. The comedy "Focker In-Law" pits Ben Stiller against Ariana Grande and looks to win the weekend with around $36 million. For what it's worth, earlier tracking (via Deadline) had both movies doing between $40 and $50 million across the five-day stretch.

In a recent development, more than A24's "Club Kid" or or the "Hershey" biopic, also releasing over Thanksgiving, it's "The Hunger Games" that will be a bigger glitch for Disney's latest. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" will be a bigger hit than you realize, doing well over $100 million on opening weekend. That means, in its second frame, it could still easily take number one over Thanksgiving.

Disney's latest centers on an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) who discovers secret magical abilities which. Once unleashed, they hurtle her out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand directed the movie, with Josie Trinidad co-directing.

The big issue for "Hexed" is that these movies don't come cheap. We're looking at a budget of at least $150 million, if not much more. Even at $150 million, an opening under $30 million across a robust, long holiday weekend is close to a death sentence. Yes, there are overseas markets to account for and family-friendly movies can have long legs. Even so, the early estimates are rough, to put it kindly.

Recent findings suggest that it's especially disappointing because this feels like the right place on the calendar for the movie. "Moana 2" smashed box office records and led to the biggest Thanksgiving ever in 2024. That eventually became a $1 billion hit for Disney. But that was a sequel to a much-beloved move from the 2010s. Originals, from both Disney Animation and Pixar, have struggled mightily in the 2020s.

In a recent development, case in point, "Strange World" bombed at the box office in 2022, taking in just $73 million worldwide. "Hexed" doesn't appear to be in such terrible shape but it's not looking good. Disney's "Wish" was also a major disappointment at the box office in 2023, doing $255 million worldwide. Decent for an original movie by today's standards but not nearly good enough to turn a profit.

Industry observers note that the only thing Disney can hope for is that word of mouth amongst moviegoers is outstanding, which could give "Hexed" unusually long legs. Or that tracking is just wildly off and the movie actually comes in closer to earlier estimates. Either way, as it stands, this one looks like it just has one too many hurdles to clear.

Disney's "Hexed" hits theaters on November 25, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amanda M. Castro is a Network TV writer at Collider and a New York–based journalist whose work has appeared in Newsweek, where she is an Associate Editor, and The U.S. Sun, where she previously served as a Senior Consumer Reporter.

According to recent reports, she specializes in network television coverage, delivering sharp, thoughtful analysis of long-running procedural hits and ambitious latest dramas across broadcast TV. At Collider, Amanda explores character arcs, storytelling trends, and the cultural impact of network series that keep audiences tuning in week after week.

Born and raised in Puerto Rico, Amanda is bilingual and holds a degree in Communication, Film, and Media Studies from the University of Latest Haven.

Romantic comedies tend to follow a familiar formula, where two people meet, fall in love, face a few obstacles, and eventually find their way back to each other. The best ones might even convince you that love can survive just about anything. But what happens when the relationship falls apart before the story really gets going? That's the question at the heart of Break Clause, a newly introduced British romantic comedy that finds plenty of laughs, awkward encounters, and genuine heartbreak in the aftermath of a breakup. Now streaming on HBO Max, the six-part series makes a compelling case for why sometimes the hardest part of ending a relationship isn't letting go. It's figuring out who gets to keep the apartment.

Industry observers note that created by Jess Bray and directed by Alice Snedden, Break Clause stars Samuel Bottomley as Ben and Lara Ricote as Lil, a young couple whose plans for a fresh start in London fall apart almost immediately. After four years together at university in Leeds, Lil lands a job in the capital and convinces Ben to make the move with her, but Ben has been keeping a secret. After a drunken indiscretion on their final night in Leeds, he eventually confesses to cheating on Lil, leaving the couple newly single just as they've signed a rental agreement.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, neither can afford to just pack up and leave. With six months of the lease to run, Ben and Lil have no choice but to become roommates, creating an uncomfortable situation where both must live separate lives while sharing a living space, kitchen, and bathroom facilities. And that's where Break Clause excels: instead of treating a break-up as the end of a romantic story, it reveals the complications that follow.

In a recent development, one of the story's strongest points is that it clearly demonstrates the ridiculousness of Ben and Lil's situation while still acknowledging the feelings beneath it. Because of this, the show can turn the storyline by focusing on two people who have already broken up instead of uniting them, as most romantic comedies usually do. They are no longer close, but they still find it hard to stop acting like a couple, at least for a bit.

Four love stories, four completely different ideas of what it means to be somebody's person. This is the one that matches how you actually fall, and what it would ask of you.

You do not fall for strangers. You fall for the person you have already been talking to for years, which is the slowest and by some distance the most durable way anybody has found to do this.

You want a partner, not an audience. Somebody who wants their own life as badly as you want yours, and who would never ask you to be smaller to make the relationship easier.

The intensity was never the problem. The secrecy is. You are drawn to a love that lives entirely in private, and to the particular ache of wanting somebody you are not supposed to want.

Sources indicate that you do not do this cautiously. When it happens for you it is immediate and total and it rearranges everything, and you would not accept a smaller version of it.

According to recent reports, notably, the idea of getting used to failure also appears inthe breakup. Generally, when people go to a different city, they think that they are starting a new chapter of life. However, Ben and Lil face unemployment and financial problems and conclude that their relationship was not as strong as they thought. The rental contract complicates the situation by creating ethical problems for everyone involved.

It has been revealed that the story's financial aspect adds another layer to the main conflict. Ben, who is trying to become a writer and struggles to find work, starts looking for food in garbage bins to save money and even considers participating in clinical research. Lil, meanwhile, has already secured a position at an architectural firm, creating an imbalance that becomes another source of tension between them. Ben’s negative attitude, tied to their financial situation, can sometimes spark arguments and problems in their relationship.

The central relationship wouldn't work without the two actors playing it. Bottomley and Ricote give Ben and Lil enough chemistry to make their shared history believable, even when they're at their least compatible. Ben is withdrawn, insecure, and often too preoccupied with his own shortcomings to recognize what's happening around him. Lil is much more outgoing, approaching life with an enthusiasm that occasionally gets her into trouble. Their personalities make for an entertaining contrast, particularly when they're forced to deal with the same uncomfortable situations.

Sources indicate that one unique performer in the cast is Ricote. She plays Lil in a way that captures the character's positive, contagious energy instead of portraying her as a peculiar person with a variety of characteristics. Although her positivity is lovable, it also creates room for mistakes. For instance, when Lil tries to attend a street dance but then realizes that nobody else is interested, it makes the character so unique. While Bottomley often explores Ben's awkwardness and embarrassment, he also indicates his attempts to reconcile with life in a ridiculous yet realistic way. Both make their characters more memorable and show why it matters whether they find a solution.

It has been revealed that there's plenty of material here beyond whether Ben and Lil will reconcile, from disastrous dinner parties to uncomfortable reunions with university friends, Break Clause finds comedy in everyday situations that become considerably more complicated when your ex is still living across the hall. Its humor can be wonderfully strange and deadpan, but Bray also understands when to give a scene space rather than turn every uncomfortable moment into a punchline.

Ben and Lil are not at home just waiting for their lease to end; they are trying to come to grips with what “growing up” means when the future they planned for no longer exists. The world around them has changed, and their friends are moving on with their careers and their lives, which makes them think about the future and their relationships with those who were once dear to them.

In the end, the series resorts to clichéd romantic comedy tropes it seems to want to avoid at the beginning, but that doesn't have to bea flaw. The mere potential for reconciliation gives the narrative an emotional arc, even as Ben and Lil navigate newly introduced relationships and increasingly muddled emotions. The issue is not only whether they still love one another but also whether they should even want the kind of relationship that they had.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I've been a fan of “Percy Jackson” for as long as I can remember. I still remember picking up the books for the first time as a kid and getting completely swept up in Rick Riordan’s world of Greek mythology, monsters and teenage demigods. It’s a franchise I’ve had a soft spot for ever since, so seeing it find a upcoming audience through Disney’s adaptation has been a real treat. And now, somehow, we’re already heading into "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" season 3. I can’t quite believe how rapidly that’s come around, but I’m certainly not complaining.

According to recent reports, season 3 adapts “The Titan's Curse,” the third book in Riordan’s beloved series. This time, Percy (Walker Scobell) and Grover (Aryan Simhadri) find themselves on a dangerous mission to rescue Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries), who has gone missing following an encounter with a mysterious upcoming threat. With the fate of Olympus hanging in the balance, Percy must contend with powerful enemies and a prophecy that could change everything. It’s another major adventure for the young demigods, but one that comes with considerably higher stakes.

I’ve watched the first four episodes of season 3, and there’s plenty to get excited about. While the show still has the humor, friendship and sense of adventure that made me fall in love with the books in the first place, this latest chapter feels noticeably more mature. It’s an encouraging step forward for the Disney+ series, and one that makes me even more invested in seeing where these characters go next. Here’s what I thought of the first four episodes.

Sources indicate that I’m Alix, a lifelong horror nerd who loves watching, reviewing and writing about the latest movies and TV demonstrates. When I’m not working through my ever-growing horror watchlist, I’m covering the biggest releases across streaming and film, including "VisionQuest" on Disney+, "The Institute" season 2 on MGM+, and "Guarding Stars" on Netflix.

Industry observers note that season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” wastes little time setting a darker, more action-packed tone. It opens with Thalia Grace (Tamara Smart) hunting for Luke (Charlie Bushnell) in a parking garage, where she finds herself battling a dangerous monster. Percy soon crashes into the fight. Thalia isn’t particularly thrilled about needing his help, which establishes some immediate friction between the two demigods. The opening also introduces the season’s central mission, with Annabeth explaining that she needs Thalia’s help to rescue two young demigods, siblings Nico (Levi Chrisopulos) and Bianca di Angelo (Olive Abercrombie).

Book readers will understand the significance of these characters straight away, while show-only viewers will get a better idea as the season unfolds. Thankfully, the first episode doesn't take long to get the main story moving, either, as Annabeth is abducted, triggering Percy’s fatal flaw: his unwavering loyalty. He’s determined to get her back, no matter how dangerous the quest becomes. That sense of danger carries through the first four episodes, and I think it’s one of the season’s biggest improvements.

With the group getting older and the looming threat of war becoming increasingly difficult to ignore, the show feels noticeably more mature in its storytelling. Percy and his friends are exposed to greater dangers, and there’s a stronger sense that their actions could have serious consequences. It’s also great to see the series developing Percy’s abilities, particularly his control over water. His powers have felt somewhat underexplored in previous seasons, so watching him become more confident and capable with them is a welcome change. He’s clearly getting stronger, and I hope the remaining episodes continue to build on that.

Of course, you can't talk about “Percy Jackson” without mentioning Percabeth, and I know plenty of fans are just as invested in Percy and Annabeth’s developing relationship as they are in the Greek mythology. Thankfully, season 3 gives us a little more to enjoy on that front. It’s still very much a slow burn, with neither quite ready to acknowledge that their feelings might be more than friendship, but there’s a growing awareness that something special is there. The dance scene in episode 1 is a particularly lovely example of this. I suspect season 3 will give Percabeth fans plenty to get excited about.

In a recent development, based on the first four episodes, season 3 is probably the strongest “Percy Jackson” season yet. I particularly appreciate is how much more attention is given to the emotional baggage these teenagers carry as the children of some incredibly powerful figures, many of whom seem largely uninterested in their own kids’ lives. including Thalia’s complicated relationship with Zeus. We get more of an insight into how these circumstances fuel their trauma and motives.

It gives the series a little more emotional depth without losing sight of the fun. The visual effects are also stronger, with the action sequences feeling grander and more cinematic than before. There’s a real sense that the show is becoming more ambitious with each season, and these early episodes have me excited to see what’s next. If the remaining episodes maintain this momentum, “Percy Jackson” could reach a whole latest level, and I can only hope Disney+ has more seasons covering the rest of the books in store.

The first two episodes of "Percy Jackson" season 3 is streaming on Disney+, with the final six episodes releasing in pairs every Friday through December 11, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In July 2026, we got an update on "Home Alone 3" (as we'll call it until further notice) that suggested Culkin's return was more likely than ever, as the actor reportedly paid a visit to the Disney lot where he met with studio head David Greenbaum.
  • According to Belloni, the "sequel/reboot" is "officially in development," with longtime writing partners Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg producing under their Point Grey banner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that arguably the greatest Christmas franchise of all time is getting its star back. 34 years after 1992's "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York," Macaulay Culkin is set to return as Kevin McCallister in a third movie that will act as a sequel/reboot for the saga.

In July 2026, we got an update on "Home Alone 3" (as we'll call it until further notice) that suggested Culkin's return was more likely than ever, as the actor reportedly paid a visit to the Disney lot where he met with studio head David Greenbaum. Now, in his What I'm Hearing newsletter over at Puck, Matthew Belloni reports that the 46-year-old actor will indeed appear in a fresh "Home Alone" movie.

According to Belloni, the "sequel/reboot" is "officially in development," with longtime writing partners Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg producing under their Point Grey banner. The report claims Rogen and Greenberg will finish up an original horror comedy project for Universal before working with Culkin on a script for the upcoming "Home Alone" film. That's good news, as the duo couldn't be better suited to the material. (Disney, of course, has yet to officially confirm any of this.).

According to recent reports, ever since "Lost in Latest York," the "Home Alone" franchise has delivered sequel after sequel that didn't need to happen — the most recent being the Mouse House's, to date, one and only attempt, following the Disney/Fox merger, to revitalize the saga with a sixth movie. But "Home Sweet Home Alone" once again failed to bring back Kevin McCallister. Now, however, things look set to change.

It has been revealed that in 2025, Macaulay Culkin embarked on a "Nostalgic Night With Macaulay Culkin" tour, during which he spoke about his surprisingly great-sounding idea for a "Home Alone 3" movie. Culkin's film would follow an adult Kevin McCallister who's become too focused on work at the expense of his young son. Kevin would then become locked out of his own house with his son still inside before having to break back in and avoid his son's ingenious traps in what is essentially a metaphor for working his way back into his son's heart. Not bad, right? For now, it remains unclear whether this is, in fact, the pitch Disney has greenlit, but it would make sense.

Recent findings suggest that culkin has seemingly been warming up to the property over the past couple of years. As mentioned, 2025 saw him launch the "Nostalgic Night" tour, during which he chatted positively about his previous two "Home Alone" movies. Then, in 2026, he played a grown-up Kevin in a McDonald's commercial. Now, pending official confirmation from Disney, it seems he'll return to the franchise proper, with Matt Belloni noting how the actor's two young sons likely played into his decision.

Belloni also highlighted the massive popularity of Culkin's first two films, which reliably shoot to the top of the most-watched streaming charts every holiday season. Per FlixPatrol, right on cue, the original "Home Alone" is back in the Disney+ movie charts, jumping from number seven on November 15, 2026, to number two as of the following day, where it sits at the time of writing. The other films in the saga? Nowhere to be seen. Lord knows the "Home Alone" movies need a major revitalization, and you couldn't do better than Culkin's return in that regard.

  • In a recent development, I couldn’t agree more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ever since Tony premiered on the 2026 movie schedule, I’ve been looking forward to rewatching it with an HBO Max subscription. That’s because it’s such a lovely and unexpectedly heartwarming film about Anthony Bourdain’s cooking origins, and I found myself wanting to hang out in Provincetown again. However, while I did that, I also learned that the director Matt Johnson and star Dominic Sessa don’t exactly feel the same way about the film, as they described making it as “being stabbed in the stomach.”.

When CinemaBlend’s Hannah Saulic sat down to chat with the cast and director of the critically acclaimed Tony, she told them she loved the movie and described it as a “warm hug.” Matt Johnson went on to say he’s actually heard this sentiment from “so many people.” And Stavros Halkias, who plays Dimitri in the movie, noted that “it is sentimental.”.

In a recent development, I couldn’t agree more. The found family element of this film is honestly quite wholesome (despite the chaos). Along with that, hanging out with Tony as he figures out his life and falls in love with cooking is a really good time. Plus, there are parts of Tony that genuinely make me emotional. So, yes, in many ways, the movie is heartwarming, because he finds his people and his calling, and who wouldn’t want to spend time watching him do that?

However, making this movie was a totally different story. Making that point very clear, Dominic Sessa, who plays Tony, and Johnson, who directed it, had this to say:.

Well, I can’t say I blame Sessa, specifically, for having this reaction. I mean, the best gag in Tony is the one where he gets splashed in the face with water over and over again. He told us that filming those scenes “sucked,” and Johnson described Sessa’s experience with this gag as “a kind of prison torture.".

So, I can see why they’d also note that filming the movie didn’t feel like a hug, and in a way felt like getting “stabbed in the stomach.”.

Industry observers note that however, again, that’s not how it reads on screen. As a movie, Tony is wonderful and not a torturous watch at all. To that point, Stavros Halkias jumped into the conversation to say:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Well, loukoumades are Greek donuts with honey, and they look delectable. And like Halkias pointed out, Tony is like a warm treat for viewers. Between Tony learning how to cook with Antonio Banderas’ Ciro, his realization that this is what he wanted to do with his life, and that Eric Ripert cameo at the end of the movie that comes with the first time Tony refers to himself as Anthony, it’s hard not to feel heartwarming energy radiating off this A24 flick.

However, when you rewatch it and feel that way, just make sure to remember and appreciate the fact that it was not that warm and cozy to make.

#62820. Who is Johannes Zuch supposed to be in GTA 6?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (985 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Polygon ↗ Open Full Page

Who is Johannes Zuch supposed to be in GTA 6?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that everyone is a target in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • According to recent reports, like previous games in the series, GTA 6 features a handful of playable games within the game.
  • It has been revealed that it’s a hysterical in-joke for those who are familiar with Blow, but it’s also a shining example of why Rockstar Games is so good at what it does.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that everyone is a target in Grand Theft Auto 6. Even Jonathan Blow, the puzzle game designer known for The Witness and Order of the Sinking Star, isn’t safe.

According to recent reports, like previous games in the series, GTA 6 features a handful of playable games within the game. (In an interview with Polygon, Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson said that the studio wanted to put some previous games in GTA 6, but the tech made that too challenging.) One of those games is Tenebrae Lux, an arthouse game filled with obtuse puzzles and pretentious monologues. It feels like a parody of The Witness right away, and that’s all but confirmed when the opening credits list its auteur developer as Johannes Zuch. Johannes is close to Jonathan, and Zuch sure sounds like “suck,” doesn’t it? Rockstar even lists Zuch as the sole creator in GTA 6’s final credits, despite the fact that it was made by a small team within the studio.

It has been revealed that it’s a hysterical in-joke for those who are familiar with Blow, but it’s also a shining example of why Rockstar Games is so good at what it does. It’s a studio that fully commits to its bits, even when it means creating a whole game to do so.

It has been revealed that you’ll first come across Tenebrae Lux early in GTA 6’s story. During a mission in Chapter 1, Cal comes over to Jason’s house to help him redecorate for Lucia’s arrival following her unexpected release from prison. After setting up the TV, Cal insists that the two take a break and play some games on the JoySystem. (Side note: If you’re playing on Xbox, there’s certainly some cognitive dissonance seeing a clear PS5 reference on screen.) He fires up Tenebrae Lux, hyping it up as a real game by a visionary developer. “He would love to work with other people, but he’s just too fucking good at everything,” Cal indicates of Johannes Zuch, whose name appears in every single opening credit as the game begins, including some comically ostentatious ones that are just outside the realm of believability, like “original idea” and “mise en scène.”.

The game itself is a black-and-white first-person puzzle game where you play as a man (voiced by Zuch, of course) who washed up on an island. As you walk around the starting area, listening to Zuch wax poetic in a highfalutin voice, you discover some scattered board game puzzles that require you to move pieces around to wipe other pieces off the board. It’s a pretty direct hit on The Witness’ brand of puzzles, where you have to learn the rules of a format without any tutorials. And it’s also a direct hit on Jonathan Blow’s brand of ostentatious writing; Tenebrae Lux sounds so much like Order of the Sinking Star (which released one month ago) that you’ll think that Blow must have had a Rockstar mole working within his studio, Thekla Inc., during development.

Recent findings suggest that tenebrae Lux only gets more obnoxious (complimentary) from there when you return to it later by playing it in Jason and Lucia’s home. The next major puzzle throws you into a series of looping, nearly identical rooms. You can only escape through a significant-brained puzzle that is so unfathomably obtuse that even a thoroughly written guide would sound like gibberish. It’s completely maddening, as Zuch won’t stop prattling on about the Sisyphean hell he’s trapped in while an old-timey sea shanty plays over and over on a crackling record player.

Recent findings suggest that as the kind of person who earnestly loves this kind of game, I will be the first to admit it: They got my ass real good. Tenebrae Lux is a pitch-perfect parody of a very specific kind of elevated art game; it’s as much a light dunk on the philosophical wandering of The Talos Principle as it is The Witness. Whether it's in good taste for a company as substantial as Rockstar to dunk on that kind of game is up to debate, but what's impressive is that it’s not a throwaway joke that’s on-screen for 60 seconds. Rockstar sells the gag by turning it into a full game that you can play at any time.

Sources indicate that that level of commitment to an out-there idea is everywhere in GTA 6. Quick visual gags turn into entire questlines. Your phone’s news app isn’t just full of goofy headlines, but fully written articles that are hysterical. Magazines are populated with feature articles that expertly ape the tone of your average grocery store glossy. Even your Instagram-like Snapmatic feed is filled with authentic shitposts and even more authentic replies. All of this gives Leonida feel like a real place with a very distinct sense of personality. If you don’t have the time to play through the entirety of GTA 6, you can understand the appeal of Rockstar’s all-in attitude through Tenebrae Lux alone.

Recent findings suggest that and if it sounds like GTA 6 is punching down on indie games, don’t worry: Rockstar takes potshots at itself and other AAA studios in the same breath. When Cal fires up Tenebrae Lux during the mission, he drops a killer meta joke as it loads. “You can see it on the screen man, it’s so fucking raw,” Cal tells Jason in a scene that very closely resembles the famous sequence from 2016’s Uncharted 4 where Nathan Drake and Elena Fisher play a round of Crash Bandicoot together. “None of just sitting around waiting for people to finish talking. Come on, are we watching a movie or playing a game here!?”.

“Cool, can we play?” a bored Jason finally indicates, cutting the chat short. I’m sure some players will feel the same after patching their roof and fixing their stairs in GTA 6’s early missions.

  • One of the District 12 kids "reaped" alongside Haymitch is Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), the daughter of a candy shop owning family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" adapts the story that fans have been waiting for since 2008, revealing how Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), future mentor of Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), became the victor of the 50th Hunger Games. Haymitch's games were even more brutal than usual: as a special "quarter quell" game, each of the twelve districts had to offer up four children, not two. (Haymitch ends up in the games after one of the two District 12 boys originally chosen tries to flee and then is shot.).

One of the District 12 kids "reaped" alongside Haymitch is Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), the daughter of a candy shop owning family. A jewelry collector, Maysilee is the original owner of the Mockingjay pin that Katniss eventually comes to wear during the "Hunger Games" trilogy.

Now, this being a prequel where Haymitch's victory (as pyrrhic as it is) is assured, you should go into "Sunrise on the Reaping" knowing Maysilee doesn't walk out of that arena. Grace actually plays two roles in the film, the other being Maysilee's twin sister, Merrilee. Once Haymitch returns, during Maysilee's funeral, he has to see the very same face of the girl he failed.

Viewers, too, might recognize Maysilee and Merrilee's shared face. Mckenna Grace is a prolific young actress with many film and TV (including voiceover) roles to her name. In just the past few years, she appeared in "Five Nights at Freddy's 2" as paranormal activity hunter Lisa, Clara in the Colleen Hoover adaptation "Regretting You," and Hannah Thurman in "Scream 7." Those recent roles only scratch the surface of her acting resume.

Born in 2006, Mckenna Grace is a recently graduated child actress; her first acting role was on the 2012 Disney XD series "Crash and Bernstein." Soon after she had a part on soap opera "The Young and the Restless" from 2013 to 2015 as Faith Newman. Her breakout film role was in 2017 Chris Evans vehicle "Gifted," where she played young math prodigy Mary Adler.

Sources indicate that in the late 2010s, Grace found a niche playing child versions of main characters. She played young Tonya Harding in "I, Tonya," young Carol Danvers in "Captain Marvel," a young Sabrina Spellman in one episode of "The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina," and starred in Mike Flanagan's miniseries "The Haunting of Hill House" as a young version of Kate Siegel's character Theo Crain. This means she's played young versions of Margot Robbie, Brie Larson, and Kiernan Shipka. (Grace, who played Paige Swanson on sitcom "Young Sheldon," has stated she envisions Reese Witherspoon as the adult version of that character.).

It has been revealed that from 2021 to 2022, during Seasons 4 and 5 of "The Handmaid's Tale," Grace played Esther Keyes, the abused teenage wife of a much older man. This role earned her an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series. 2021 was also the year that Grace starred in "Ghostbusters: Afterlife" as Phoebe Spangler, later reprising the role in 2024's "Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire.".

One of Grace's voiceover roles was playing a young version of Daphne Blake in the 2020 animated "Scooby Doo!" film "Scoob!" Fresh off of "Sunrise on the Reaping," she's going to play Daphne again, this time in live-action, in the upcoming TV series "Scooby Doo: Origins" due out in 2027.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is playing in theaters.

Recent findings suggest that looking for a genuinely cool tech gadget for less than $25? I’ve got just the one. The Casio WSB1000-1AV is a tough-built digital watch beaming with 1990s charm, but also a surprising smattering of modern tech niceties. Best of all, it’s 65% off for Black Friday.

Need an office Secret Santa/gift exchange option that won’t break the bank? Not sure what to get for your “cool” Gen Z cousin or technologically challenged parents? The answer is this deeply discounted $22 Casio watch, which, on pretty much any other day, would cost you $64. Here are five reasons why.

Marked down from $64 to just $22, this retro-1990s Casio digital watch features an onboard step counter and Bluetooth antenna for automatic time adjustments.

It has been revealed that hidden behind the screen of this seemingly ordinary digital watch is a Bluetooth antenna. Why would a dumb watch need Bluetooth? To pair it with your smartphone, of course. Once paired, the Casio WSB1000 automatically corrects the time based on your smartphone’s clock.

Recent findings suggest that this means there’s no need to fuss with resetting the time when traveling across time zones. The bare-bones smartphone app can also be used to set or cancel an alarm on the watch, a timer, a stopwatch, and other basic functions.

Lastly, the onboard Bluetooth plays a key role in this next feature.

Industry observers note that you’ll notice that the Casio WSB1000 has the words “Step Tracker” printed above the LCD. This refers to this little watch’s automatic step-counting feature. Who needs the best Apple Watch or the latest Fitbit?

Industry observers note that like an actual smartwatch or fitness tracker, consumers can set daily step-count targets. The WSB1000 not only tracks your total and displays it on the watch’s LCD, but it also shows a dynamic graphic of your progress toward that day’s goal.

Bluetooth, meanwhile, is used to ping that step-count data back to your smartphone.

With onboard Bluetooth and automatic step-count tracking, battery life must be pretty short? Surprisingly, no. Casio notes that the common drugstore CR2016 battery in the watch should keep it powered for approximately two years.

Afterwards, a battery swap should be a relatively painless, affordable process, done either at home (if you're savvy) or at your local jewelry store.

Sources indicate that while the Casio WSB1000 isn’t quite as durable as watches in the brand’s legendary G-Shock range, this digital wonder is rated for 100 meters of water resistance, the same as the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4. It also boasts a shock-resistant (though not shockproof), lightweight resin case.

Ultimately, for less than $25, you're not just getting a Bluetooth-capable digital watch with step counting; you're getting the Casio WSB1000, a 90s timepiece with a design that's Tom Cruise-running-atop-a-moving-train-cool; it's Keanu Reeves-stopping-a-speeding-bus-badass... etc.

And even if your intended recipient overlooks the step tracking and tosses this watch in a drawer for occasional use, when they do eventually pull it out and pop it on, you can be sure the time and date will be spot-on thanks to the Bluetooth connection.
