Following last month’s launch of the iPhone Duo, which also saw the release of Apple’s official repair manuals for the device, Apple today began selling replacement parts and tools through its Self Service Repair Store. Here are the details.

Since 2022, Apple has offered its Self Service Repair program, allowing owners in eligible regions to purchase replacement parts and buy or rent the tools needed to perform their own repairs on supported devices.

Just a few weeks ago, Apple began offering replacement parts and tools for several recently released devices, including the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, the latest Mac Studio, and the Mac mini.

Today, the firm also added the iPhone Duo to the list, allowing owners and independent repair technicians to purchase the necessary replacement parts to perform repairs on the device themselves.

It has been revealed that in addition to these and other replacement parts, Apple also offers the tools and other supplies needed for each repair procedure. These include adhesive cutters, suction cups, nylon probes, adhesive removal tools, torque drivers, and screws, all of which can also be purchased separately.

For consumers looking for guidance on performing these repairs, Apple also offers detailed, step-by-step repair manuals, which the company released on the same day the iPhone Duo debuted last month. #62794. Industry News: Walter Hill on Sam Peckinpah, Steve McQueen, and His Revolutionary Screenplay for ‘The Getaway’

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1473 w)

Industry News: Walter Hill on Sam Peckinpah, Steve McQueen, and His Revolutionary Screenplay for ‘The Getaway’

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1473 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 1972, Walter Hill was a young screenwriter with just one produced movie (“Hickey & Boggs”) behind him when he scored an enviable gig: adapting Jim Thompson’s tough-as-nails crime novel “The Getaway” for actor/producer Steve McQueen (then one of the biggest movie stars in the world) and director Sam Peckinpah (then, as now, one of the greatest directors who ever lived).
  • “The Getaway” screened as part of the museum’s “Branch Selects” series, in which the Academy’s various branches program films they feel exemplify their crafts.
  • According to recent reports, “ Walter, right off the bat, changed the art of screenwriting,” Karaszewski mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 1972, Walter Hill was a young screenwriter with just one produced movie (“Hickey & Boggs”) behind him when he scored an enviable gig: adapting Jim Thompson’s tough-as-nails crime novel “The Getaway” for actor/producer Steve McQueen (then one of the biggest movie stars in the world) and director Sam Peckinpah (then, as now, one of the greatest directors who ever lived). On Wednesday night, Hill spoke before a packed screening at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures and looked back on the movie that jump-started not only his screenwriting endeavors, but a directing career that would ultimately include classics like “The Warriors,” “48hrs.,” and “Streets of Fire.” Related Stories Short Film ‘Lightning Bug’ Gives Stage and Screen Legend Lois Smith One of Her Greatest Roles — Watch It Here Is A24 Finally Big Enough to Be Considered a Major Studio?

“The Getaway” screened as part of the museum’s “Branch Selects” series, in which the Academy’s various branches program films they feel exemplify their crafts. “The Getaway” was, appropriately enough, selected by the writers branch, and screenwriter and Academy Governor Larry Karaszewski was on hand to introduce the movie and moderate the pre-screening discussion with Hill. Karaszewski, a longtime “Getaway” enthusiast who carried newspaper ads from the movie around in his wallet when he was 10 years old, pointed out that Hill changed the entire architecture of screenwriting when he burst onto the scene in the early 1970s.

According to recent reports, “ Walter, right off the bat, changed the art of screenwriting,” Karaszewski mentioned. “We have an award show here at the Oscars called the Sci-Tech Awards, where they give awards to things that silently change the industry and advance them into the future. I really feel that Walter Hill did that in screenwriting, but it wasn’t a technical advancement. It was a literary advancement. He changed what a page should look like as a screenplay and what it could feel like to read it.” Karaszewski went on to illustrate his point by projecting pages from Robert Bolt’s “Doctor Zhivago” screenplay and Walter Hill’s “Hard Times” side by side on the screen.

Sources indicate that “You don’t even have to read [Bolt’s script], just look at it,” Karaszewski stated, pointing out the dense blocks of words compared to Hill’s lean, spare page. “You’re looking at monoliths. It’s dense, and there are camera moves and references to things you would never see on screen. Walter Hill taught screenwriters that you can strip all that away. You can still direct on the page, but not by calling for specific camera movements — just by saying what you’re seeing. Walter’s scripts are made out of short sentences and white space. He looked at the placement of each line as part of the storytelling. He turned the carriage return into an art form.”.

As Karaszewski welcomed Hill to the stage, he pointed out that “The Getaway” — a smart, terse tale of a couple (Steve McQueen and Ali MacGraw) on the run after their involvement in a botched bank robbery — represented the emergence of Hill’s developing voice. “You’ll already see the beginnings of that remarkable style, the economy, the precision, the sense that every line is pushing you toward the next image.” Yet, as Hill revealed in his lively conversation with Karaszewski, the ruthless efficiency of the pacing and the concentrated emotional impact of “The Getaway” were not easily arrived at.

“I think it’s much harder to adapt than it is to write an original, which is the reverse of the normal theory,” Hill mentioned. “With an original, it’s just you at your desk with the typewriter or pen. When you’re adapting, that almost always means that somebody else owns it, so you’re not simply writing based on your own opinions about what should be in and what should be out, but there’s the producer’s opinion, and the studio’s, and the actor’s. There were all these political currents that one had to navigate.”.

One such political current came from megastar McQueen, who didn’t interfere much with Hill’s writing but did have one caveat that amused the screenwriter. “He wanted to play a reasonably sympathetic outlaw,” Hill said. “That was not in the Thompson sensibility. So we already had a disparity, but the producer wanted to keep Steve happy.”.

In a recent development, “The Getaway” began as an assignment not for Peckinpah, but for Peter Bogdanovich, who was white-hot coming off of successes like “The Last Picture Show” and “What’s Up, Doc?” Bogdanovich didn’t last long, however, given his clashes with McQueen and McQueen’s power as the film‘s star. “I couldn’t imagine two more diverse sensibilities than Steve and Peter,” Hill remarked, noting that he had his own disagreements with Bogdanovich over the movie’s tone but wasn’t in a position to argue. “You’ve got to remember, I was nobody. I had one screen credit. And these were big players.”.

In a recent development, the major players included not only Bogdanovich and McQueen, but MacGraw, hot off of the smash hit “Love Story.” MacGraw was pushed into the movie by her husband, Paramount studio chief Robert Evans, which Hill found amusing given the way everything played out. “I’m going to tread lightly here,” Hill noted of the behind-the-scenes melodrama involving MacGraw leaving Evans when she fell in love with McQueen. “When the material was optioned and I was hired, Bob saw the movie as a fabulous idea for Steve and Ali. It didn’t work out so well for him.”.

After Bogdanovich and McQueen butted heads, Bogdanovich was let go and Peckinpah, who McQueen had enjoyed working with on “Junior Bonner,” came in to take his place. “We were very lucky to get such a talented guy, obviously,” Hill mentioned. “I thought of him then and I think of him now as one of the great directors with a very unique sensibility. I was very privileged to work with him — which doesn’t mean he and I agreed about everything.”.

According to recent reports, hill’s biggest disagreement with Peckinpah had to do with a scene in which MacGraw’s character considered killing McQueen before turning the gun on his nemesis — and the man with whom MacGraw had gone to bed to secure McQueen’s early release from prison. This was a scene carried over from the book, which was darker and more paranoid than what made it to the screen given McQueen’s mandate that he be sympathetic. Hill felt that the moment no longer worked now that the relationship between McQueen and MacGraw was softer and more relatable in the novel.

Industry observers note that “I thought that for the movie we were trying to make, you might forgive your wife for sleeping with a bad man to do a very good thing for you,” Hill said. “That seemed to be to be conceivable. But if your wife fell into cahoots with the bad guy and actually was thinking about killing you and actually turned the gun on you before she decided to shoot the other guy…this did not track for me. But this is the screenwriter’s dilemma: you either talk the director into your point of view, or you make the change that he wants — or somebody else will. Those are your choices.”.

Hill lost the argument but liked the movie Peckinpah made in the end. “He staged it beautifully,” Hill remarked. “He shot it beautifully. It’s got one of Steve’s best performances. And the movie turned out to be his greatest hit. He used to call me every once in a while after I became a director and say, ‘Write me another one.'” Ironically, it was the success of “The Getaway” that put Hill in a position where didn’t have to write for other directors anymore.

“Larry Gordon had a producing deal to make low-budget movies at Columbia,” Hill noted. “He would give young writers a chance to direct, because he said, ‘Even if they’re no good as directors, at least we’ll get a good script. Most of the directors I’m working with aren’t any good anyway.'” Gordon gave Hill the opportunity to direct “Hard Times,” and the rest was history. Aside from kicking off Hill’s directing career, the collaboration became the first of many between the two men. “He’s a wonderful guy and a wonderful producer.”.

Sources indicate that now in his 80s, Hill continues to write and direct (his last film was the exquisite character-driven Western “Dead for a Dollar“), plying his trade in the world of graphic novels in between film projects. “I’ve had four of them published in France,” Hill mentioned, joking that the only one published in America was “the least good of them,” but promising another one on the way. “You’ve got to keep your hand in somehow.”.

How to hide the latest macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (327 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar.
  • I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override. Apple describes itas a transparency indicator that appears when one app is controlling another.

Recent findings suggest that if you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar. Prefer to hide it? There’s a Terminal workaround.

I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.

Open Terminal and run these two commands:.

sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false.

Enter your Mac administrator password when prompted, then restart your Mac.

Sources indicate that the command disables the internal AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR feature flag. It doesn’t remove apps from your permissions list, although you’ll no longer see this activity indicator.

To restore Apple’s default behavior, run:.

sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR.

Industry observers note that restart your Mac again to apply the reversal. This removes only the indicator override, preserving any other flags you may have configured.

This is an undocumented workaround tested on the current beta, so Apple could change or remove it in a future enhancement.

According to recent reports, not a fan of this on macOS 27.3 beta 2. Terminal command + reboot removed.sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false pic.twitter.com/HVvWdInqPh.

Do more with your Apple products.

I did offer alternatives like backing to your Mac or external SSD, but to have a proper backup safety system you need 1-2 backups at home and one off site (ie. friends house, storage facility, etc.) and you would have to be consistent with your backups and drop offs. Most people don’t have the time so they do iCloud, same as I.

In a recent development, similar to Apple’s other AI usage limits, your access to the Cloud Pro model in Shortcuts increases if you have a higher storage strategy. Per this support document, the 200GB plan supports standard limits, the 2TB plan offers 5x access, followed by 10x on the 6TB plan and 20x on the 12TB plan.

iCloud+ already provided far more than just increased cloud storage, but with iOS 27.3 it’s set to be an asset for AI power users too.

‘Josephine’ Review: Another Heartsick Horror Film About Real Monsters from ‘Soft & Quiet’ Filmmaker

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on January 23, 2026 during the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.
  • According to recent reports, at this point, filmmaker Beth de Araújo is two for two.
  • More concisely: with her “Soft & Quiet” and “Josephine,” de Araújo remains undefeated when it comes to making stunning films that I will both heartily recommend and never, ever watch again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on January 23, 2026 during the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Sumerian Pictures will release the film in limited theaters on Friday, November 20, with a wide release to follow on Friday, December 4.].

According to recent reports, at this point, filmmaker Beth de Araújo is two for two. Not just in terms of the quality of her films — impeccably crafted fever dreams of very different stripes and horrifyingly similar themes — but in how these films make the viewer feel.

More concisely: with her “Soft & Quiet” and “Josephine,” de Araújo remains undefeated when it comes to making stunning films that I will both heartily recommend and never, ever watch again. Related Stories Walter Hill on Sam Peckinpah, Steve McQueen, and His Revolutionary Screenplay for ‘The Getaway’ Short Film ‘Lightning Bug’ Gives Stage and Screen Legend Lois Smith One of Her Greatest Roles — Watch It Here.

The word that comes to mind when watching a de Araújo feature is heartsick. That applies to the feeling bestowed on both the audience and her characters (the good guys and the bad guys). While her first film, the unrelenting “Soft & Quiet,” was cleverly designed to appear as if it was shot in a single real-time take, her sophomore feature is more about the steady accumulation of dread. The heroines of “Soft & Quiet” recognize what they are dealing with almost immediately (the force of the evil that is bent on destroying them is what’s surprises most), but the star at the center of “Josephine” is not just wounded by the sickness that suddenly infiltrates her young life, but her complete lack of understanding about what is happening to her and why.

In both films, it’s not just bad deeds that upends everyday lives, it’s real evil, actual monsters, perversions that don’t only show up in a movie screen. That’s true terror.

According to recent reports, based loosely on an experience de Araújo, who both wrote and directed the film, experienced as a child, “Josephine” initially lulls us into a false sense of safety. It’s early morning in San Francisco, and fledgling soccer star Josephine (Mason Reeves, riveting in her first role) is getting ready for a run with her devoted dad Damien (Channing Tatum, bringing incredible girl-dad energy to the role). It’s something the pair do every Sunday morning: get up early to watch Premier League football, run through a woodsy neighboring park, and kick the ball around.

Sources indicate that for her second film, de Araújo leans less on clever camera tricks, though she and cinematographer Greta Zozula occasionally put us in Josephine’s own perspective, shooting as if we are looking through the eight-year-old’s eyes. As with “Soft & Quiet,” the gimmick works, grounding us in Josephine’s world and immersing us, if briefly, in what the world looks like from her vantage. Jo-Jo, as her dad calls her, is plucky and fun and filled with energy, so when she briefly zips ahead of her dad while on their run through Golden Gate Park, it just seems like everyday high-jinks.

Recent findings suggest that but when the path forks (about as heavy-handed a metaphor as de Araújo will ever employ), Josephine goes to the left, while Damien goes to the right. What she finds there will forever alter the course of her life, and set “Josephine” off on a heart-wrenching journey with no easy answers. Curious and watchful, Josephine ducks behind a tree when she sees a woman (Syra McCarthy) running into a public bathroom at the bottom of a scrubby hill, and she sinks even further down when a young man (a bone-chilling Philip Ettinger) follows the unknown woman into the tiny building.

It has been revealed that de Araújo’s approach to portraying on-screen violence only furthers that heartsick feeling: straightforward, unsparing, and absolutely devoid of any possibility of being compared to “torture porn.” What we see, what Josephine sees, is something no person should ever witness or experience. And that’s the root of the film’s power: how do we talk about things that we should not have words for?

When Damien arrives on the scene, it kicks off what will become one of Tatum’s best performances yet, a deep-feeling and heartbreaking exploration of layers of emotional unease. Damien does everything “right,” ensuring both Josephine and the woman are safe, chasing after the assailant, calling the cops, a neat little checklist of “how to handle an emergency.” And yet, the damage has already been done. There will be more to come.

Even when Josephine begins to seek out answers to what she’s seen (snatching her mom’s phone to search “raip,” reeling at what she discovers), it’s impossible to make sense of everything. There are things to fear she never even know existed, and the deep-seated powerlessness that overtakes her causes her to act out in chilling and increasingly volatile ways. Her parents’ reactions don’t help: her exceedingly calm mother Claire (Gemma Chan, thrilling as a character just barely holding it together) wants her to see a therapist now, her more action-oriented dad is eager to put her into self-defense classes. The mixed messages both give off (to say nothing of their own barely concealed terror) do little to help Josephine, who soon becomes someone almost entirely different than the care-free kid she just was.

She also picks up a fresh friend: Ettinger begins to appear to her, a literal haunting figure, never saying a word, yet barging into nearly every moment of Josephine’s already upended life. It’s the sort of choice another filmmaker fight fill tricksy or silly, but that de Araújo delivers with the maximum of impact. And that we, like Josephine and only Josephine, can see him only furthers our immersion into her world. It almost goes beyond empathy.

According to recent reports, josephine’s steadily unfolding breakdown is only compounded by the arrival of yet another situation no eight-year-old should ever have to encounter: handling the messy investigation of the crime itself. How she might help (or not) drives one more wedge between Josephine and her parents, who all have a different take on what the “right” thing to do is.

If these questions sound heady and heavy, they are, but de Araújo’s masterful ability to interrogate tension on every level keeps the film clipping along, each turn both a surprise and an inevitability. The monsters are here, they are real, and they’re coming.

“Josephine” premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO shook up the AI market and US economy last week, but now via The Wall Street Journal Huang has spoken out publicly for the first time since stepping down, and he signals he’s ready to return as CEO if asked.

Today Robbie Whelan at The Wall Street Journal published Jensen Huang’s first public statement since departing Nvidia last week.

According to recent reports, “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the manufacturer, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

In a recent development, to be clear, I’m also willing to step in as CEO of Nvidia if asked. I’ve owned several generations of their graphics cards, so I have plenty of experience with their products. More importantly, this is probably my best chance of finally having enough cash to afford a Mac with 32GB of RAM.

The timing is likely no coincidence, as Nvidia is set to report its quarterly earnings later today.

Even though Huang technically resigned as CEO rather than being fired, it was clear that his ouster wasn’t exactly his choice. Thus, today’s statement is the former CEO formally putting it out into the world that he’s ready to return if asked.

Since Huang stepped down, President Trump publicly called on Apple’s Tim Cook to step in as Nvidia CEO. But it’s expected that a fresh CEO—assuming it’s not Huang—will take much longer for the company to find and Cook is unlikely to want the job.

Industry observers note that ““The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” earned $21 million in Thursday previews and early screenings on Wednesday and is expected to dominate the box office this weekend. Analysts believe it will earn north of $100 million. The preview figures are the second-best of 2026, behind “Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day’s” massive $72 million haul. It’s also the second-best for the “Hunger Games” franchise, just behind the $25.5 million that “Catching Fire” earned in 2013. It’s a massive improvement on the last “Hunger Games” prequel, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” which made $5.75 million in previews and kicked off with $44 million. That film would gross over $166 million domestically and nearly $364 million globally, figures that “Sunrise on the Reaping” is on pace to easily eclipse.

Industry observers note that “Sunrise on the Reaping” is based on Suzanne Collins’ bestselling novel of the same name. It tells the origin story of Haymitch Abernathy, the alcoholic former Hunger Games victor played by Woody Harrelson in the films. The sequel checks in with him at 16 as he’s forced to compete in gladiatorial combat. “East of Eden” breakout Joseph Zada plays Haymitch. He’s surrounded by an all-star cast that includes Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace, and Maya Hawke. Francis Lawrence, who helmed most of the series’ films, returns as director. Lionsgate, which is having a strong year at the box office thanks to “Michael,” is backing the “Hunger Games” sequel as it has the previous films.

The biggest competition for “Sunrise on the Reaping” this weekend isn’t another major movie, but the release of “Grand Theft Auto 6,” which is expected to be a phenomenon.

#62779. 9 Video Game Sequels Better Than the Original

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1874 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Collider ↗ Open Full Page

9 Video Game Sequels Better Than the Original

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In theory, sequels should always be better than the original since it is easier to see the flaws of the first and correct them.
  • According to recent reports, that is why this list will feature eight video game sequels that are better than the original based on aspects such as improvements, design, gameplay, narrative, originality, fan opinion, critical acclaim, and overall quality.
  • According to recent reports, games on this list don’t specifically need to be the second game in a franchise, as long as they are a sequel, which opens the door for Baldur’s Gate 3.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In theory, sequels should always be better than the original since it is easier to see the flaws of the first and correct them. However, sometimes it’s too difficult to capture the certain magic that the first title had, and this is especially true for video games like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. However, that isn’t always true, with some sequels not only living up to the hype, but also becoming better video games.

According to recent reports, that is why this list will feature eight video game sequels that are better than the original based on aspects such as improvements, design, gameplay, narrative, originality, fan opinion, critical acclaim, and overall quality. These games took the base of something great and made it even better, becoming the definitive version and a sequel that improved on almost everything. Please note that Red Dead Redemption 2 will not be on this list because it is a prequel, not a sequel.

According to recent reports, games on this list don’t specifically need to be the second game in a franchise, as long as they are a sequel, which opens the door for Baldur’s Gate 3. When the player is infected by a Mind Flayer parasite, they will turn into one if they don’t find a cure for themselves. Teaming up with others in their position, gamers travel across the country in search of this concoction, but the brewing war between gods and mortals makes this much more complicated.

In a recent development, baldur’s Gate 3 is the most recent game on this list, but it didn’t take long to become one of the most influential titles of all time. This is the ultimate role-playing experience, improving on the narrative, scale, gameplay, graphics, and options. Baldur’s Gate 3 is as good a sequel as it can get, even if this entire franchise is home to masterpieces. There is so much love and passion put into this game, and fans can feel it in every ounce of the design, which is exactly what every sequel should have.

Batman is one of the biggest superheroes of all time, with his presence extending from comics to movies and even video games. Batman: Arkham City puts Bruce Wayne into the titular prison, which is a walled-off section of Gotham City. Donning the cap and cowl, players must learn of Protocol 10, the mysterious strategy Hugo Strange has set, but first, Batman needs to take care of the many villains trying to kill him.

In a recent development, batman: Arkham Asylum is a fantastic game, but most fans will agree the sequel is much better. The open-world allowed for more engaging traversal, the narrative was tenser and had fewer errors, and the gameplay was extended with more combos, making it one of the best martial arts video games. It is the perfect follow-up to an already incredible video game, arguably establishing itself as the definitive Batman experience not just in video games, but overall.

Resident Evil is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, with massive projects such as Resident Evil Requiem and the film directed by Zach Cregger. However, nothing can compare to Resident Evil 4, the best sequel in the franchise. When the daughter of the president is kidnapped by a cult in Spain, Leon S. Kennedy goes to save her. But when he learns the cult has been infected by a parasite, survival and escape become even more difficult.

Industry observers note that the first Resident Evil is great, but most of the sequels are better than it, especially Resident Evil 4. While polarizing to some, the changes made in Resident Evil 4 revitalized the franchise, adding stylish action mechanics and an over-the-shoulder camera view. It was simple, but very effective, making this game way easier to play than other titles while maintaining the core difficulty and fun. Resident Evil 4 is a horror masterpiece and a sequel that is one of the best games ever.

It was recently announced that EA shut down BioWare, the game studio that brought fans so many classics, including the Mass Effect franchise. Each game is nearly perfect, but Mass Effect 2 in particular stands out as one of the best. Years after the first game, Commander Shepard is killed in the line of duty, only to be revived shortly after. Those who brought him back to life task him with investigating a mysterious alien race that has abducted entire human colonies, harvesting people to build a newly introduced threat to the entire galaxy.

Sources indicate that the first Mass Effect was a terrific video game that established the beloved formula, and this sequel took what was great in that and expanded on it. The first bright spot is the fact that progress from the first game is saved in the sequel, creating an interconnected feel that makes decisions long-term. Mass Effect 2 strips away the original inventory management, repetitive exploration, and stiff shooting, replacing them with improved mechanics and design for a much better experience. With the gameplay greatly improved, it could then focus on what the franchise is best known for: the worldbuilding, which is what makes Mass Effect 2 one of the best sci-fi video games for beginners.

Assassin’s Creed is one of the best historical video game franchises of all time, and while it has changed its formula to be more mythological and open-world RPG, the roots of historical stealth are unmatched, and that is highlighted by Assassin’s Creed II. Set in Renaissance Italy during the late 15th century, the story follows Ezio, a young Florentine nobleman whose father and brothers are framed for treason and publicly executed. He dons his father’s assassin robes and embarks on a quest for vengeance against those who wronged him, including the Templar Order.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to superior sequels, Assassin’s Creed II is a textbook example, transforming the foundation into a player-driven experience. Adding mission variety, this mix of tasks built a much better experience in terms of gameplay, and set in the gorgeous Renaissance cities, it was a true joy to explore. Ezio is also regarded as the best protagonist in the franchise, and it isn’t hard to see why, providing a decades-spanning character arc that shows his entire evolution. Assassin’s Creed II is a complete overhaul that creates the quintessential game in the franchise.

The Witcher franchise is at an all-time high, with a TV show adaptation, upcoming DLC, and a sequel, which all started because of the popularity of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Geralt of Rivia is a Witcher, but he must put aside his usual monster-hunting gig in order to save Ciri, his adoptive daughter, from the titular spectral group that wants to use her powers for evil.

According to recent reports, when talking about The Witcher, most fans just ignore the first two since they didn’t play them. And while they are good, they don’t hold a candle to the third game. The combat can be better, but the worldbuilding and narrative more than make up for that. Lore and details spawn in every corner of the map, with side quests starting as something simple and then evolving into a grand yet personal tale. Not to mention, monster hunting is a pure delight that forces players to be tactical, proving why it is one of the best video games of the 2010s and better than its predecessors.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

Sources indicate that you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Grand Theft Auto is arguably the greatest video game franchise of all time, and if there was any doubt, it disappeared after Grand Theft Auto VI came out to glowing reviews. Bringing gamers back to Vice City decades later, they control dual protagonists, Lucia and Jason, a couple who work their way through the chaotic city from common thieves to a criminal power couple.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI is officially the highest-rated video game of all time, meaning it is clearly better than its predecessors. While some fans will disagree, there is no denying that the hype paid off, delivering an incredibly rich world of crime, freedom, and chaos. The sheer detail in every corner of Vice City is astounding, and beyond looking gorgeous, GTA VI is the most mechanically deep in the franchise, proving why it is the definitive GTA sequel.

While the most recent Street Fighter movie was critically panned, the sequel has a good chance of being better since the original Street Fighter II is the best game in the franchise. M. Bison hosts an international fighting tournament that brings in the strongest brawlers from around the world, all competing to test their might and win the ultimate prize, but there might be some ulterior motives behind this competition.

In a recent development, the fighting genre, as gamers know it, was built on the back of Street Fighter II, which not only improved the franchise but gaming as a whole. The added combo system became a staple in virtually every game going forward, and the improved graphics, controls, and combat variants made gameplay infinitely more engaging. There aren't many fighting games better than Street Fighter II; it's just a pity the franchise peaked this early.

Valve is one of the greatest video game studios ever, and it seems they have a knack for sequels, with a couple of masterpieces, such as Half-Life 2 and Portal 2. The latter is set years after the first, with Chell waking up to the same facility, except this time it is falling apart. Working with a friendly robot, she attempts to escape the facility, but the reawakening of GLaDOS makes this more challenging.

Portal 2 is an amazing game from start to finish that takes the base of the first game and builds something entirely new on top of it. This game makes the first look like a vertical slice because of the sheer details, expanded gameplay, narrative, and scale. The co-op mode also offers a fun multiplayer experience and new ways to play. Portal 2 isn’t just better than the first game, but it may be the greatest game of all time.

#62777. 25 Best Enemies To Lovers Manhwa Ever

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Screenrant ↗ Open Full Page

25 Best Enemies To Lovers Manhwa Ever

📅 28 Apr 2024 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1911 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Romance manhwa comes in many forms, but some of the most memorable love stories begin with two people who would rather have nothing to do with each other.
  • Sources indicate that the enemies-to-lovers trope is especially popular in fantasy and otome isekai manhwa, where political intrigue, second chances, arranged marriages, and complicated family histories provide plenty of opportunities for romantic conflict.
  • It has been revealed that beastly Things has a distinct Twilight vibe, introducing readers to a secret society of werewolves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Romance manhwa comes in many forms, but some of the most memorable love stories begin with two people who would rather have nothing to do with each other. Whether their animosity stems from conflicting ambitions, family rivalries, painful misunderstandings, or circumstances that force them into an uncomfortable partnership, these stories thrive on the tension between their protagonists. Watching two characters gradually abandon their resentment and discover an unexpected connection is one of the most satisfying aspects of the enemies-to-lovers genre.

Sources indicate that the enemies-to-lovers trope is especially popular in fantasy and otome isekai manhwa, where political intrigue, second chances, arranged marriages, and complicated family histories provide plenty of opportunities for romantic conflict. However, the trope isn't limited to historical settings or villainess reincarnation stories. From dangerous games of manipulation to hilarious workplace rivalries and relationships built on long-standing grudges, there's something for every romance fan. For readers who enjoy watching hostility gradually turn into affection, these manhwa are well worth adding to their reading lists.

It has been revealed that beastly Things has a distinct Twilight vibe, introducing readers to a secret society of werewolves. The story follows Ji-u Han, the pack leader's daughter, who harbors an inferiority complex and resents her father for not choosing her as his successor. The plot kicks off when she meets the actor Yuseung Cheo, who's actually a werewolf hunter seeking to exact revenge on the race that killed his parents. However, Ji-u also intends to use him to secure the power she so deeply craves.

Featuring a series of human murders in addition to the conflict between werewolves and hunters, the webtoon's true appeal lies in its two manipulative protagonists on opposing sides, secretly playing games with one another while inevitably beginning to develop feelings. While it features all the hallmarks of toxic relationships, such as obsession, betrayal, and hidden agendas, Beastly Things proves to be an addictive guilty pleasure that's hard to put down.

The Crown Princess Scandal is a different kind of enemies-to-lovers story, as it sets aside the angst and drama in favor of absurd interactions and protagonists whose only reason for hating each other is their clashing personalities. The webtoon begins with Hwa-Yeong, who reluctantly takes her sister's place in a selection process to become the crown princess.

Hwa-Yeong just wants to go home, and the crown prince finds satisfaction in not letting her get away with her looks, with the plot delivering all sorts of hilarious bickering between the two. Although it feels more like a simple comedy at first, the humor doesn't overshadow the romance, and even Hwa-Yeong’s antics serve as a catalyst for the characters' emotional growth. The palpable tension between the protagonists and the way their relationship develops make The Crown Princess Scandal an especially cute and lighthearted love story.

The Hand That Once Fed offers a particularly messy interpretation of enemies-to-lovers romance, exploring what happens when a former relationship deteriorates into resentment and a desire for revenge. The story follows Evelyn Winter, a widowed duchess whose seemingly comfortable life is disrupted when Colonel Gilath Black suddenly returns. Once her devoted servant and lover, Gilath now approaches her with accusations of treason and an entirely different attitude toward the woman he once adored.

Industry observers note that what makes this relationship particularly compelling is the dramatic reversal of their former positions. Gilath, who was once loyal to Evelyn, has become a dangerous presence in her household, while Evelyn must fight to protect her position and navigate the consequences of their shared history. Neither character is particularly straightforward, and their interactions leave readers questioning whether Gilath wants to rekindle their relationship or destroy the woman who once held his heart. With its exploration of betrayal, obsession, and unresolved feelings, The Hand That Once Fed is an excellent choice for readers who prefer their romances with plenty of psychological tension.

Recent findings suggest that betrayal of Dignity is a dark historical romance that puts its protagonists in a complicated relationship defined by manipulation, desperation, and conflicting interests. The story follows Chloe Verdier, a young noblewoman struggling to prevent her family from falling into ruin. When her sister Alice disappears with a mysterious man, Chloe finds herself turning to Duke Damien Thisse, a notoriously arrogant and ruthless military hero. His proposal offers a potential solution to her family's problems, but accepting his help means entering a dangerous arrangement with a man she can hardly trust.

Industry observers note that unlike lighter enemies-to-lovers stories, Betrayal of Dignity doesn't shy away from the uncomfortable aspects of its central relationship. Damien's controlling personality and Chloe's determination to protect herself create an ongoing struggle for power, with neither protagonist willing to surrender easily. Chloe is particularly interesting because she isn't simply swept away by the Duke's wealth or appearance; she has her own priorities and must constantly consider the consequences of her decisions. The result is an emotionally complicated romance filled with questionable choices, courtly intrigue, and a relationship that is anything but straightforward.

According to recent reports, frozen Hearts introduces a supernatural variation of the enemies-to-lovers trope, placing its protagonists on opposite sides of a dangerous conflict. The story follows Seolha, a Snow Maiden demon who has concealed her true identity while living among humans. Her carefully maintained disguise becomes increasingly difficult to protect when she attracts the attention of the Northern Prince, a man infamous for hunting and killing demons. Their circumstances eventually lead to Seolha becoming his bride, creating an unusual marriage between two individuals who should naturally be enemies.

In a recent development, the main appeal of Frozen Hearts comes from the secrets and conflicting loyalties surrounding its protagonists. Seolha must conceal her identity while navigating married life with someone whose reputation makes him particularly dangerous to her kind. Meanwhile, the prince must contend with a relationship that challenges the rigid beliefs underlying his demon-hunting activities. Their situation creates plenty of opportunities for suspicion, emotional conflict, and gradual character development. With its winter-inspired fantasy setting and supernatural premise, Frozen Hearts is an especially appealing choice for readers who enjoy watching characters from opposing worlds develop feelings for each other.

Dear Nemesis offers a very entertaining take on the enemies-to-lovers trope, combining reincarnation, aristocratic politics, and a romance built on a complicated history. The story follows Calmia Phlox, who receives a second chance at life after a previous existence that left her determined to reclaim her family's position and secure her future as Countess Phlox. However, her ambitions become complicated when she must compete with her beloved twin brother while navigating the schemes of those around her. Matters become even more interesting when Rudbeckia Matari, her former archenemy, unexpectedly proposes marriage.

In a recent development, rather than immediately abandoning their differences, Calmia and Rudbeckia approach their engagement as a calculated arrangement, with both having their own ambitions and reasons for accepting the partnership. Their shared history makes it difficult for either to place complete trust in the other, but their political alliance gradually develops into something much more personal. With two intelligent, ambitious protagonists constantly trying to stay one step ahead of each other, Dear Nemesis delivers an especially satisfying slow-burn romance. Its combination of strategic maneuvering, family drama, and gradually developing affection makes it an excellent choice for readers who enjoy seeing former rivals become unexpected romantic partners.

Act Like You Love Me! approaches enemies-to-lovers romance with a considerably lighter touch, combining workplace comedy, celebrity culture, and an unexpected supernatural twist. The story follows Ji-eon, a 25-year-old woman struggling financially while juggling demanding jobs. An unexpected temporary assignment puts her in the position of assisting Doyun Nam, a famous actor whose demanding personality quickly gets on her nerves. After another frustrating encounter, Ji-eon discovers that a seemingly ordinary doll possesses the bizarre ability to control him.

In a recent development, suddenly, the power dynamic between the two changes completely, giving Ji-eon an opportunity to turn the tables on the celebrity who has made her working life miserable. However, having control over someone and actually understanding them are two very different things. As their interactions become increasingly complicated, the hostility between Ji-eon and Doyun gradually develops into something neither initially expected. The series balances its romantic development with plenty of humorous situations, making it a refreshing alternative to the darker, more emotionally demanding stories associated with the trope. For readers who enjoy workplace romances, bickering protagonists, and unconventional premises, Act Like You Love Me! is an entertaining addition.

In a recent development, as its title suggests, Your Eternal Lies follows a deceitful and morally gray protagonist. In the webtoon, Rosen Walker is a notorious criminal who has successfully escaped from prison twice before falling under the supervision of war hero Ian Connor. Thus, Your Eternal Lies mixes the best of the enemies-to-lovers trope with a sort of cat-and-mouse police hunt aboard a ship that keeps readers in suspense about whether she will manage to escape, as well as the real nature of the charges brought against her.

The story features fantasy elements, such as the existence of witches, yet it also offers a grounded reflection on death and the consequences of war, centering on layered characters, each with their own traumas. Beyond the instant chemistry between the protagonists, Your Eternal Lies plays out like a complex game of chess, with Rosen being a wonderfully cunning and strong female lead, making it quite difficult not to root for her to win.

In a recent development, adonis, also known as Reminescence Adonis, puts an interesting spin on the enemies-to-lovers trope. Ianna, an expert swordfighter, has already spent one lifetime being Arhad's enemy. Her only goal was to best him in battle, but she failed to accomplish even this. Though Ianna claims she has no regrets, as she teeters on the brink of death, she hopes that she can be reborn as Arhad's knight and ally instead of his enemy in her next life. Fortunately, Ianna's dying wish is heard, and she finds herself in the body of her younger self when she opens her eyes.

The deep, almost obsessive love that eventually develops between Arhad and Ianna also offers plenty of payoff.

Sources indicate that though Adonis does take its sweet time with the romance, the series' engaging characters more than make up for the slow burn. The deep, almost obsessive love that eventually develops between Arhad and Ianna also offers plenty of payoff, making this series an absolute must read, especially for fans of historical romance manhwa.

Recent findings suggest that an especially impressive take on the Snow White fairy tale, Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom is a saccharine and wholesome redemption story for Abigail Freidkin, the iconic evil stepmother. It's essentially a blend of isekai and enemies to lovers, where Baekhap Lee, an overworked children's fashion designer, dies from overwork and reincarnates as Abigail. She quickly embarks on a quest to dote on her daughter, Princess Blanche, while evading icy-cool tensions with her estranged, hostile husband, Sabrian.

Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom is loaded with endearing quirks, such as Abigail's unique villainess quality, where she smiles an inherently malevolent smile even when happy, bewildering her servants and husband. Yet, she muscles through it due to her adoration for her daughter. All the while, Sabrian's hostilities include sabotaging Abigail's gifts for Blanche, believing them to be ill-intentioned, yet maintaining a mere distance from her without outright divorcing or showing intentions to remarry, stoking immediate anticipation for sparks to begin flying between them.

#62776. Why Do AI Posters All Look Like That?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1274 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Why Do AI Posters All Look Like That?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every poster for a business or event has pictures of uncanny-looking people, buildings that don’t look right, and always that one font.
  • At this point, gone are the days of chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini simply generating text immediately in response to a prompt.
  • To borrow a classic and implausible example, if you were to give an AI chatbot the instruction “Make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich,” it would start by generating step-by-step instructions on how to make the sandwich before trying to make one (if it could).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know “the look” by now. Every poster for a business or event has pictures of uncanny-looking people, buildings that don’t look right, and always that one font. But why? If generative AI is supposedly able to “think” and be “creative,” why do so many of its results come out looking exactly the same? The answer is complicated, and it has to do with what chatbots define as “thinking.”.

At this point, gone are the days of chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini simply generating text immediately in response to a prompt. Some very fast models do, but most employ what’s known as “thinking models”, which are a bit of a misnomer. The “thinking” really just consists of generating a set of sub-prompts before executing the main one. And it’s in that hidden, generated text that most of the “choices” (to the extent that we can call the statistical output of an AI model a “choice”) occur that determine how a design looks.

To borrow a classic and implausible example, if you were to give an AI chatbot the instruction “Make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich,” it would start by generating step-by-step instructions on how to make the sandwich before trying to make one (if it could). Most of this happens invisibly in the background, and many proprietary chatbots won’t show you their in-process “thinking” prompts even if you ask.

In the case of an AI poster, it might break down “make a poster” into smaller steps such as “create a design brief for a poster.” To demonstrate this while doing some testing for this piece, I added additional prompts for ChatGPT to explain the “design briefs” it generated, which included details like layout, colors, and typography.

Recent findings suggest that the problem is those instructions are still subject to the same flaws as any other AI-generated text. They can’t properly fact-check; they can’t walk into the real world and see the thing they’re describing; and they can hallucinate or fall back on stale formats that become easy to notice after a while.

For example, while testing, I had ChatGPT generate a poster for a Lifehacker-themed nightclub. In every case, the underlying brief it generated outlined some basic details, but occasionally it added things I hadn’t asked for. This included additional text, iconography, and in one case it even added the “design brief” explanation I had requested as the bottom half of the poster.

Those mistakes filter into the final product, when the brief is then fed into the image generator that ultimately makes the poster. In my case, ChatGPT showed me the underlying explanations for its reasoning (though even that could be different from what was actually sent to the image generator), but most people who use a chatbot for this task won’t see these factors before getting the final result.

While most chatbots won’t show you exactly what underlying “thinking” they use, most can be coaxed into describing the vague outlines of how they reached certain outcomes. And those descriptions provide some insight into why certain chatbots keep outputting similar results over and over. It doesn’t take long for some patterns to emerge. For example, any prompt to generate a poster for a nightclub almost invariably generated a brief that had specifications for a color palette including “electric purple,” “electric yellow,” and “electric pink.”.

It has been revealed that the reason for this should be pretty obvious: When the statistical model underlying LLMs needs to come up with an example for “colors for a nightclub poster,” the most obvious answers are neon, high-energy colors. Unless you know something about the specific club’s vibe (and write that out and feed it to the chatbot), the AI will have to fill in the gaps with something. And that something will be based on the same statistics it uses to predict any word.

This pattern of repetition was everywhere in all the design rationale ChatGPT gave me. Across multiple attempts to generate a Club Lifehacker poster, the generated design brief added an overarching “concept” that described the fictional club’s atmosphere as “high-energy” and “futuristic.” Every bot mentioned using images with the “silhouette” of either the DJ or a dancing crowd (often both). All the text had to be “bold” and “futuristic.".

Recent findings suggest that if there's one dead giveaway that a poster was made with AI, it's that one brush-stroke font that they all seem to use. Now, this is a bit more speculative, but I have a theory on where that specific design comes from. And it’s worth noting upfront that this seems to only apply to posters generated by ChatGPT specifically.

Sources indicate that one of the most common factors I found in my design brief testing was the use of phrases like “brush lettering” or “brush script.” Brush lettering is a design term that refers to using any number of methods like markers, paint brushes, or brush pens to write text. In digital design, that can take the form of fonts that are designed to emulate the look of fancy, handwritten text.

In every test poster I created, however, ChatGPT seemed to take the phrase “brush lettering” rather literally. Every instance I encountered of a design brief that mentioned any kind of “brush” text generated an image with letters that looked as though they were created with a broad paint brush. A human designer would understand “brush lettering” to mean “something that looks handwritten," but ChatGPT didn’t seem capable of understanding the phrase as anything other than using an actual paint brush.

Industry observers note that the generated posters aren’t even using a “font,” strictly speaking. (Often, letters that should be identical had slight variations.) The image generator part of the chatbot is still a diffusion model, so it can’t employ a vector-based font, per se. But the brush-style font is so common that its look surfaces in any statistical model.

This is an odd quirk of ChatGPT specifically, and it’s possible that it could change in the future. Especially if OpenAI intentionally tries to train this behavior out of its chatbot. However, it’s helpful to illustrate the underlying mechanism. The only way a chatbot can conceptualize design elements in a visual medium is to generate more specific text to feed to the image generator. And that text is just as prone to mistakes and blandness as any other AI model.

I’ve been examining this with a focus on the kinds of posters ChatGPT generates because they’re very common, but posters (or any AI-generated content) from other models might look different. Every model has its own tendencies. For example, a lot of vibecoded websites are made with Anthropic’s Claude, and you can often tell by the tiny text, buttons with rounded corners, and tile-based layouts.

To a certain extent, this is inevitable. While AI models are very different from humans and do not make “choices” in the same way people do, design elements still have to come from somewhere, and whether human or AI, it’s impossible to make these decisions in a vacuum. Humans will have preferences based on the things they like or emotionally resonate with, and AI models will have tendencies based on what their statistical model determines is the most appropriate output.

That means that an AI model’s “style” is naturally going to change over time. Even if a model improves or makes fewer mistakes, it’s impossible to ever change the fact that all ChatGPT images are made by ChatGPT. Whatever you generate with any particular model will have a lot in common with what everyone else who uses the same tool generates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on October 2, 2026 during the 2026 New York Film Festival. Janus Film will release the film in limited theaters on Friday, November 20.].

Paul Thomas Anderson‘s eye for vivifying music onscreen dates back to the late 1990s when, after “Boogie Nights,” he made Technicolor mini-masterpiece music videos with his ex-girlfriend Fiona Apple — or made a San Fernando Valley-sized shrine to Aimee Mann with his third feature, “Magnolia.” Since then, he’s kicked around with HAIM while turning one third of its Los Angelino triumvirate, Alana Haim, into a screen actress. He’s shot for Radiohead and made a regular collaboration with band member Jonny Greenwood to create some of the 21st century’s most memorable scores. Many young cinephiles now associate the mischievously lilty notes of “Phantom Thread” with the poison promise of newly introduced love and obsessive creation. Related Stories Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Scores $21 Million in Previews, Second-Best Result of 2026 ‘Josephine’ Review: Another Heartsick Horror Film About Real Monsters from ‘Soft & Quiet’ Filmmaker.

According to recent reports, last December, PTA teamed up with Geese frontman Cameron Winter to film, while operating his own Panavision camera, his solo stage performance at Carnegie Hall, running through sparse piano arrangements of tracks off his solo album, “Heavy Metal.” The result, a 72-minute film now being distributed roadshow-style by Janus Films before inevitably living on the Criterion Collection, is a stunning arrangement of its own: a deeply achey, sincere but never cloyingly earnest concert movie that’s tender to the point of frailty. (Benny Safdie counts as a co-producer, and the film’s scratchy New York quality and setting can’t help but have his imprint.).

In a recent development, the matted-hair, lithe Winter can seem a bit uncomfortable in his own skin in the public eye, as he did onstage ahead of “Cameron Winter at Carnegie” at its Fresh York Film Festival world premiere at Alice Tully Hall. But on the piano, laser-beamed into his songcraft, he’s quietly electrified, at seemingly at peace as his tenorous vocal glissando and nimble fingerwork on the piano produce shiveringly tender folk ballads that echo Harry Nilsson and Van Morrison. (The usual comparisons to Tom Waits and Rufus Wainright are right, too, but Winter is his own strange thing.) If you weren’t previously sold on the wily Winter antic rock chaos of Geese — rapidly becoming one of the most popular contemporary art rock bands of these times — you’re about to. Paul Thomas Anderson has created a rhapsodic shrine to the man that is nonetheless ballad-sized in its emotional scale.

Sources indicate that winter, in December, played and sang to a sold-out crowd of more than 2,700 at the stately cultural temple that is Carnegie Hall, and this film can at times feel like a religious experience, an incantation, a lonely vigil. The singer/songwriter was 23 at the time of the performance, one year older than Bob Dylan when he headlined Carnegie Hall, and similarly at the precipice of major fame. Fixed on a mobile rig that will at times careen and whoosh across the stage when not otherwise holding on Winter, Anderson’s camera catches the expressionism and chiaroscuro of stage lights illuminating and fading off the singer’s face.

The result is hynoptic, a concert film up there with “Stop Making Sense” but for introverts. Songs like the popular single “$0” acquire an even more wrenchingly somber quality as a lovelorn protagonist rues being exploited by a relationship (“You’re making me feel like a dollar in your hand / You’re making me feel like I’m a zero dollar man”). Stripped of production, his indie hit “Love Takes Miles” plays even better. While many of the songs sort of hover in the same key and bleed into one another, that makes for an all the more transfixing experience. The lack of an interstitial anything save for a sweet prologue and moving coda make for experience also that’s immersive, deep, and the kind whose truth you can feel somewhere in your body even if you can’t quite articulate it.

“Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall premiered at the New York Film Festival. Janus Films will release it in theaters starting November 20.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the firm’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside latest features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

Professional and amateur photographers just got a newly introduced alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the manufacturer’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the tech giant’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing users to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:.

It has been revealed that “Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

The first thing customers will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

In a recent development, as for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Consumers can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the manufacturer’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for swiftly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

Recent findings suggest that and speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow users to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are newly introduced organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow customers to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, owners can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

According to recent reports, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:.

With tasks, Google’s “goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.” Google shared use cases like:.

With today’s announcement, Google is emphasizing that “Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because [your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards] already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.”.

Behind the scenes, Gemini tasks work in your own “hardware-isolated virtual machine” that’s sandboxed and has protections against prompt injection, while leveraging Google Safe Browsing when browsing the web.

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.”.

Powered by the fresh Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

What ‘Digger’ Has in Common with Gary Oldman’s Winston Churchill and Charlize Theron’s Megyn Kelly

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tom Cruise‘s performance in Alejandro González Iñárritu‘s “Digger” is one of the boldest and most entertaining of the actor’s career, as he suppresses not only his usual movie star charisma but his entire way of walking and talking to play paunchy, aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell.
  • To aid in his complete transformation, Cruise called on one of the best prosthetic designers in the business, Kazu Hiro.
  • “Alejandro is an amazing director, and he has lots of ideas,” Hiro told IndieWire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tom Cruise‘s performance in Alejandro González Iñárritu‘s “Digger” is one of the boldest and most entertaining of the actor’s career, as he suppresses not only his usual movie star charisma but his entire way of walking and talking to play paunchy, aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell. Cruise is barely recognizable in the role, which is about as far from heroic characters like Pete “Maverick” Mitchell and Ethan Hunt as Cruise’s Ron Kovic in “Born on the Fourth of July” was from race car driver Cole Trickle almost 40 years ago.

To aid in his complete transformation, Cruise called on one of the best prosthetic designers in the business, Kazu Hiro. Hiro has turned Gary Oldman into Winston Churchill (“The Darkest Hour”), Charlize Theron into Megyn Kelly (“Bombshell”), and Dwayne Johnson into “Smashing Machine” Mark Kerr, but transforming Cruise into Texas oilman Digger Rockwell was a whole new task — one made even more challenging by Iñárritu and Cruise’s persistent striving for perfectionism, and constant eagerness to try new approaches. Related Stories ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Review: PTA’s Spellbinding Concert Doc Is a Gorgeously Tender Performance Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Scores $21 Million in Previews, Second-Best Result of 2026.

“Alejandro is an amazing director, and he has lots of ideas,” Hiro told IndieWire. “Every day he comes in with a new idea, and we have to come up with an answer for how to achieve it. And Tom is really professional, and expects everybody else to be at that same level, ready for any situation. After the first day of testing, I learned that I had to stay flexible to respond to whatever they wanted.”.

To that end, Hiro created modular prosthetics whose parts could easily be swapped out and moved around, so that Cruise and Iñárritu could constantly try new looks. “Sometimes with heavy makeup, you can’t change it,” Hiro said. “I created prosthetics that could be mixed, so we could make new designs on the spot — try this forehead with these cheeks and this nose, then change it.” Creating Cruise’s look was a constantly evolving process throughout the long prep period. “We didn’t have a clear answer until the end of rehearsal.”.

Hiro’s mandate at the beginning was a bit open-ended, which gave him room for artistic exploration but also made it difficult to zero in on a precise look. “Alejandro said the character was 76 years old and an oil tycoon,” Hiro said. “He also said he didn’t want the character to look like Tom, but he still wanted to see Tom in the character.” To try to find a concrete image for Digger Rockwell, Hiro immersed himself in research.

“I researched real oil tycoons and how they aged and what kinds of lifestyles they had,” Hiro said. “Those lifestyles affect how they age.” As Hiro did more and more research, however, he realized that there was no one look that defined the entire profession he was trying to represent. “Everybody looked so different, so in the end I relied more on the storyline and how this particular character behaved.” The idea, in keeping with the slightly heightened style of the film as a whole, was to exaggerate Cruise’s features but keep the character realistic.

It has been revealed that hiro began with a 3D scan and life cast of Cruise, which he used to sculpt his designs. His paramount concern was allowing the actor to be as expressive as possible under the makeup. “The key part is to make the prosthetic very soft so he can move,” Hiro noted, noting that three weeks before shooting, Iñárritu called with a significant change. “He decided that Digger should be 65, not 76, so I rapidly made a fresh design. Tom is around that age, but he looks much younger than a normal 65. Under his eye was exposed and the rest of the face was covered, but I made it thin to give him freedom.”.

In addition to Digger’s face, Hiro was also tasked with creating an upper body for an early scene in which Cruise would be seen stripped down to his pajama pants. The body prosthetic was intended only for that one scene, with a lighter bodysuit created for the rest of the movie. “We made a light version of the padding for under the costume, because we don’t need to see the skin after that first scene,” Hiro noted. “For the first scene we made a silicone prosthetic that was a lot heavier — the body padding was around 10 pounds, but the silicone was 40 or 50.”.

During one of Cruise’s costume fittings, he told Hiro he wanted to feel the weight of the silicone throughout production. “He tried the body prosthetic on and stated, ‘I like this, I want to wear it every day,'” Hiro said. “I told him it would be really heavy and hot, but he said he was training and would be fine.” Since gluing the body prosthetic on every day would be extremely time-consuming, Hiro created a strong spandex foundation and glued the prosthetic to it so Cruise could slip it on each day.

Industry observers note that “He wore that for the whole film,” Hiro said. “One time he said, ‘This is so heavy, it’s really hard on my back.’ I thought, ‘Okay, you asked for it,’ but he went through with it and finished the film, so that was amazing.”.
