📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aqara has declared the global launch of six newly introduced smart lighting products with full Apple Home support and what the company describes as “spatial intelligence.”.

The fresh lineup includes a vertical floor lamp with 18 individually addressable lighting zones, and a new LED strip offering seamless color gradients, dynamic flowing effects, and music synchronization ….

All of the new products are Matter compatible, allowing them to fully integrate with Apple Home, in addition to supporting the full range of competing ecosystems: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings, Home Assistant, and Homey.

With a compatible sensor like the FP400, all of the newly introduced products support spatial intelligence.

This enables automation to respond not only to whether someone is present, but also to exactly where people are within a space and how they move through it. For example, the ambient lights can turn on and off based on your movement from the couch to the dining room table.

According to recent reports, its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

In a recent development, you might initially struggle to spot the new products in the company’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

Pricing ranges from $24 for new light bulbs through to $320 for the 100-foot-long permanent outdoor rope lights. You can find all the new products here.

#62699. Breaking: Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1159 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1159 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • According to recent reports, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

According to recent reports, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

According to recent reports, you can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Sources indicate that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

In a recent development, file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Recent findings suggest that game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

In a recent development, according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

According to recent reports, first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

It has been revealed that also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

In a recent development, if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

Sources indicate that more importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

In a recent development, the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.
  • VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out.
  • The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial patch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial patch.

On Android, this comes in the form of fresh color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “My only memory of music growing up was getting in the car and listening to my dad’s CDs, and John Mayer was his guy,” Warren remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for country chart-topper Megan Moroney and pop hitmaker Alex Warren, a song isn’t necessarily finished when it leaves the studio. Sometimes, it needs a test drive.

For Warren, listening to music in the car holds sentimental meaning. On his new album, Wildchild, he pays tribute to his late father, who died of cancer when Warren was just nine years old. Some of his most powerful musical memories with his dad are inseparable from time spent in the car.

“My only memory of music growing up was getting in the car and listening to my dad’s CDs, and John Mayer was his guy,” Warren remarked. “When my dad passed away, I got in his car and [Mayer’s album] came on. When I wrote this song for my dad called ‘Wildchild,’ I put his voice on it, and I asked [Mayer] to do a guitar solo on it, so my dad and John have a song.”.

According to recent reports, the car is also where Warren discovered Moroney’s music. He recalls listening to her breakout hit “Tennessee Orange” in the car with his wife, who knew every word.

“She knows that song like the back of her hand, and it’s really cool because she applies it to her own life,” Warren said of Moroney’s autobiographical debut, which tells the story of a die-hard Georgia football fan falling for a Tennessee Volunteers fan.

“It encapsulates the kind of music my fans like,” said Moroney, whose sharp-eyed songwriting turns specific details into universal feelings that resonate with the masses.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s creative, it’s honest, there’s the hook, and it’s storytelling. I feel like at the root of all of my songs, that’s what it is. And obviously I’m a Georgia Bulldog, so it’s just very me.”.

Moroney and Warren may come from different corners of the music world, but the two found plenty of common ground during a conversation outside Fox & Locke, a storied live-music venue tucked into the rolling countryside of Leiper’s Fork, Tennessee. The discussion was part of Rolling Stone’s Musicians on Musicians series. This time, Lexus sought to connect two artists from different backgrounds in an entirely newly introduced way by trading the usual lounge-like venues that host Musicians on Musicians conversations for the lounge-inspired quiet cabin of an all-electric 2027 Lexus TZ, which will make its debut this winter. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, as the conversation continued, Moroney and Warren learned that their paths to stardom have more than a few parallels. Both got an early boost from TikTok before breaking through with massive singles from their debut albums — Moroney with her five-times-platinum “Tennessee Orange,” Warren with his record-breaking “Ordinary.” Both have crossed genre lines through collaborations, and both released hit albums this year: Moroney’s autobiographical Cloud 9 and Warren’s deeply personal Wildchild. They also share a belief in one essential part of the creative process: the all-key “car test.”.

For Warren, that test played a pivotal role in one of the biggest songs of his career. After receiving an early, stripped-down version of “Ordinary” — little more than his voice and a piano — he played it for his wife while they were driving. Her reaction told him everything he needed to know. “She was like, ‘I want more of it!’”.

Industry observers note that the experience changed the way he shares newly introduced music. “Now I only show people songs in my car.”.

He might be onto something. Whether you’re a professional musician or more of a carpool-karaoke type, there’s something about hearing a song on the road that changes the experience. A lyric lands a little harder. A melody feels a little bigger. And sometimes, the right song at the right moment can turn a daily drive into something worth remembering. Cosmetics’ ‘Mirror Mix’.

It helps when the sound system is up to the task. The all-electric Lexus TZ features an available 21-speaker Mark Levinson audio system, engineered specifically for the TZ’s three-row cabin to deliver the kind of rich, immersive sound that feels the way it was meant to be heard.

Of course, when your life revolves around music, sometimes the best soundtrack is no soundtrack at all. For artists like Moroney and Warren, who spend much of their time on the road, a long drive can also offer a rare chance to unplug, catch up, and simply have a conversation. The TZ makes room for both experiences, and that balance between sound and silence feels particularly fitting for two artists who know a song’s power to make a personal story resonate far beyond its original inspiration.

It has been revealed that it’s a reminder that the songs we carry with us are rarely just about the music. They’re tied to people, places, and moments that stick around long after the last note fades. And sometimes, the best way to know whether a song really works is to get behind the wheel, turn it up, and see where it takes you.

In a recent development, leaker Ice Universe notes Apple is presently developing four models of the 20th anniversary iPhone which we’ve been referring to as the iPhone 20. We’re expecting next year’s flagship models to be a radical newly introduced design with an all-glass appearance.

Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product ….

Didn’t the iPhone 6 or the iPhone 11 already have a curved front glass?

Ice Universe indicates that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.

Apple is currently developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.

It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of newly introduced devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.

We’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report notes the bezels are around 1mm thick.

Sources indicate that the curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.

We yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.

It has been revealed that black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a major discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

Recent findings suggest that if you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is presently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink promptly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

Industry observers note that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Latest Update: After 5 hours with GTA 6, I’ve already made 3 major mistakes — here’s how to avoid them

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait.
  • Like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro.
  • So, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait. Not only is the Vice City map absolutely huge, but it’s the most system-rich and mechanically deep game in the Grand Theft Auto series to date. There’s an overwhelming amount of things to see, do, and learn.

Like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro. I’ve since put five hours of playtime into GTA 6, and while I’m still getting my head around all that the game has to offer (my completion percentage is a mere 12%), I’ve already learnt a few lessons the hard way. Yes, mistakes have been made.

So, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free). Learn from my errors!

After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 introduces a fresh money system in which you can hold cash either on your person or stashed securely at your safehouse. If you get “wasted” or “busted” by the cops, you’ll lose all the money you’re carrying, but the funds kept under the floorboards at Jason's beachside home are protected.

It has been revealed that as a cautious type, I took this to mean never carry any money on your person for fear of losing it, which pretty quickly proved to be an oversteer when an early mission required me to buy a gun, and I literally had $0 in my wallet. This forced a trip back to the safehouse, where I counted out the exact number of bills required to buy the weapon.

Sources indicate that once I returned to the Ammu-nation store, I bought my gun and then was presented with a range of attachments (some with a limited-time discount), which I couldn’t buy because, again, I’d only brought the specific amount required to buy the gun itself. Frustrating.

Recent findings suggest that this taught me not to fear actually carrying money in your wallet. Sure, running about Vice City with your entire bank balance on hand is probably unwise, but you’re going to want, and need, some money in your pocket. At this early stage, I’ve been opting for a 50/50 split, keeping half my ill-gotten gains in my stash, and the other half within instant reach.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

My approach to previous GTA games tended to be this: Complete a few story missions, and then go on a psychotic rampage to blow off some steam (I swear I’m not a total psycho).

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is different. For pretty much the first time in the franchise’s history, the game actively discourages you from causing carnage without purpose through the newly introduced “Criminal Profile” system. Your in-game actions are tracked and contribute to the type of criminal Jason (and later Lucia) is becoming. Ranging from a “professional” all the way to a full-blown “psycho.”.

During my first GTA 6 session, after completing the mandatory prologue, I decided to see how many wanted stars I could rack up with just the starter pistol, and pretty rapidly the game warned me that my criminal spree would have consequences. It felt like that old Tellale’s The Walking Dead warning message, “Clementine will remember that…”.

Rockstar has confirmed your “Criminal Profile” will impact how the story plays out, and I certainly don’t want to receive a “bad” ending; such was my concern about how my early game rampage would impact how my GTA 6 story plays out, I opted to reload to a previous save to instantly wash away the worrying amount of blood already on Jason’s hands.

So, in GTA 6, it pays to show restraint. You will commit many crimes, of course, but resist the urge to go full GTA and instead commit your criminal acts with purpose and even planning.

Speaking of planning, from what I’ve played so far, GTA 6 is the most ambitious Grand Theft Auto yet in all areas, including mission design. Previous GTA games present players with cinematic but largely linear missions; if you tried to get creative, the game would quickly shepherd you back onto the golden path with instant fail states for any deviations.

To be clear, GTA 6 does have these types of missions as well, but there’s a larger focus on player choice and letting you pick your approach. As an early (spoiler-free) example, a Chapter 1 mission asks you to retrieve a red sports car from a police impound lot.

You’re dropped off right outside the main gate, with an on-screen prompt encouraging you to break the lock. Naturally, I obliged, and the impound’s alarms started blaring; every cop in the area was instantly alerted, and the mission pretty much went further south from there.

One reload later, I was back at the mission start, and this time, I slowed down. I cased the joint first, walking the perimeter, trying to find a subtler way to access the impound lot. And what do you know, a conveniently placed scissor lift around the corner got me onto the roof, allowing me to quietly drop into the compound without setting off any alarms or alert cops.

It’s a reminder that in GTA 6, thinking before you act can pay off, and when you factor in the “Criminal Profile” system, there is real merit in completing missions without having to shoot your way out of trouble.

The G1 Garbage Collector

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Garbage-First Garbage Collector (G1) is the default garbage collector on the JVM as of JDK 27, with JEP 523: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector in All Environments, which made it the default in all environments.
  • In a recent development, G1 was originally introduced in JDK 6u14 as an experimental feature, promoted to a standard feature in JDK 7u4, and designated the default garbage collector in JDK 9, taking over that role from ParallelGC.
  • In a recent development, at the time of its introduction, G1 was designed for server environments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Garbage-First Garbage Collector (G1) is the default garbage collector on the JVM as of JDK 27, with JEP 523: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector in All Environments, which made it the default in all environments. It had been the default garbage collector in "server" environments since JDK 9, with JEP 248: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector. G1 seeks to balance throughput and latency and is a good option for many workloads. In this article, we will cover a brief history of G1, its key design concepts, and how to use it.

In a recent development, G1 was originally introduced in JDK 6u14 as an experimental feature, promoted to a standard feature in JDK 7u4, and designated the default garbage collector in JDK 9, taking over that role from ParallelGC. While G1 has taken over the role of default garbage collector from Parallel, it was originally introduced to replace the CMS (Concurrent-Mark-Sweep) Garbage Collector, which was deprecated in JDK 9 and removed in JDK 14.

In a recent development, at the time of its introduction, G1 was designed for server environments. Systems using G1 were expected to have multiple processors and large amounts of system memory (tens of GB) available. Continued development of G1 has reduced its system requirements, and now G1 can provide good performance even in resource constrained environments with only a single CPU and less than 2 GB of available system memory. This is why, as of JDK 27, it is the default garbage collector across all system configurations.

In garbage collector design, the three primary design constraints are throughput, latency (pause time), and memory footprint. G1 seeks to maintain a balance between latency and throughput, rather than heavily optimizing for either. By comparison, ParallelGC primarily focuses on maximizing throughput, and ZGC focuses on minimizing latency. G1 also aims for more consistent pause times than the CMS collector it replaced.

As of the writing of this article, 12 JEPs relating to G1 have been delivered since JDK 8, with more changes planned for the future. Continued development has steadily improved G1's throughput, latency, and memory footprint.

G1 is a generational, incremental, parallel, mostly concurrent, stop-the-world, and evacuating garbage collector. For an explanation of each of these terms, check the Garbage Collection Concepts and JVM Collectors article on dev.java. This section covers some of the key design characteristics of G1.

Sources indicate that as mentioned in the previous section, G1 was originally designed with large "server-like" environments in mind. G1 is capable of efficiently marshalling the resources of systems with dozens of cores and addressing heaps measured in tens of GB.

Figure 03-01: Simplified representation of the G1 heap layout.

Recent findings suggest that G1 divides the heap into a set of regions (increments) of uniform size. Figure 03-01 is a simplified example of what the G1 heap space would look like. The size and number of regions, unless otherwise configured, are based on internal heuristics, with the overall heap size being the primary influence on both. These regions are then divided up into eden, survivor, old, and humongous regions.

Recent findings suggest that eden and survivor regions are both part of the "young" generation. On creation, an object is placed in an eden region. If that object survives a collection, it is evacuated (copied) into a survivor region. Unreachable objects are not deleted individually; rather, the region they are a part of is considered empty and is eligible for reuse by G1. Surviving objects, if they remain reachable, will be evacuated to a latest survivor region on subsequent collections. If an object survives enough collections, based on internal heuristics unless otherwise configured, it will be evacuated to an old region, which is checked less frequently.

According to recent reports, A humongous region is a contiguous space of one or more regions, reserved for a single "humongous" object. An object qualifies as "humongous" if it's larger than half the size of a single region. Humongous objects bypass the eden and survivor regions and are treated as equivalent to an old region by G1.

Figure 03-02: Simplified representation of the G1 garbage collection cycle.

Industry observers note that the G1 garbage collection cycle (GC cycle) consists of both stop-the-world and concurrent behavior, both of which can run in parallel. Again, check Garbage Collection Concepts and JVM Collectors for definitions of these terms. Figure 03-02 is a simplified visualization of the G1 GC cycle and will help to contextualize this section.

In a recent development, at a high level, the G1 GC cycle consists of two phases: Young-Only and Space-Reclamation. G1 will start in the Young-Only phase, which, as the name suggests, means only young regions are collected. In G1, when a collection happens, the application is paused while G1 evacuates objects to latest regions or performs other GC work.

The concurrent behavior of G1 is primarily concerned with determining which objects in old regions are still active. The concurrent phase can be broken into three distinct parts and starts when old-generation occupancy reaches a threshold.

Sources indicate that concurrent Start is the first step in the concurrent phase and is a special pause. During this pause, normal evacuation of young regions still occurs, and G1 also initiates concurrent marking of old-generation regions to determine which objects are still reachable. It is also possible that G1 determines there is no need to follow through with marking, in which case a Concurrent Mark Undo pause occurs, and the Young-Only phase continues.

In a recent development, remark is the second step in the concurrent phase. This is a special pause where no evacuation of young regions happens. Instead, during this pause, G1 finalizes concurrent marking and performs other work, such as reference processing, class unloading, and reclaiming empty regions. Between this phase and Cleanup, G1 will concurrently calculate information to be used during the Space-Reclamation phase.

Sources indicate that cleanup is the third and final step in the concurrent phase. This is also a special pause where no evacuation of young regions happens. During this pause, G1 determines if it should proceed to the Space-Reclamation phase. If a Space-Reclamation phase is determined to be necessary, the Young-Only phase will complete with a single Prepare Mixed young collection.

In a recent development, the Space-Reclamation phase consists of multiple mixed collections: collections where young and old regions are evacuated. G1 uses an efficiency algorithm to determine which old regions to collect first. A major factor in this algorithm is the amount of garbage in each old region, as regions with more garbage are more likely to yield large amounts of space. This is what "Garbage-First" in the G1 name refers to: it will reclaim the regions with the most garbage first.

According to recent reports, the Space-Reclamation phase ends when G1 determines that evacuating more old regions is no longer worth the effort. At this point, G1 shifts back to the Young-Only phase.

For more technical details on G1, check the Garbage-First Garbage Collector guide and the G1 Stack Walker video at the bottom of this page.

G1 is explicitly enabled with the JVM argument -XX:+UseG1GC. If you are on JDK 27 or later, this argument is never necessary, as G1 was designated the default GC in all environments. From JDK 9 to JDK 26, G1 was chosen by the JVM if it detected two or more CPU cores and more than 1792 MB of available system memory; otherwise, SerialGC was used. If you are on JDK 8, you will need to explicitly set -XX:+UseG1GC to use G1, as ParallelGC is the default GC.

Recent findings suggest that generally speaking, users should avoid applying too much configuration to garbage collectors. Often, "less is more," and the engineers who develop and maintain garbage collectors, G1 included, have worked toward having internal heuristics provide the best performance in most use cases "out of the box." As of the writing of this article, an upcoming change to G1, Automatic Heap Sizing, would handle one of the most notable remaining aspects of G1 configuration: configuring the heap size.

When thinking about configuring a garbage collector, consider the three major constraints garbage collectors are designed around: throughput, latency, and memory footprint. G1 aims for a balance between latency and throughput. When a user provides custom configuration to G1, some tradeoff will be happening. A user increasing the heap size is trying to trade a larger memory footprint for reduced latency. A user setting a higher pause time goal for G1 will be trying to trade reduced latency for improved throughput. As a user considers configuring G1, there are no settings for simply "better" performance, but, at best, a tradeoff. Some configuration combinations simply lead to worse observed performance. Below are some key configuration parameters for G1.

For a deeper dive into configuring G1, check the guide maintained by the G1 engineering team.

Recent findings suggest that the album’s August release date marked two milestones: the first time a member had released solo music and the first release since Adam Yauch (aka MCA) died in 2012 of cancer. Speaking to Rolling Stone earlier this year, Mike D reflected on what it took to make an album for the first time without Yauch and Adam Horovitz (aka Ad-Rock) by his side.

“With Yauch, there was so much intertwined about him being an older-brother figure to me, to what he represented to us being in this band together,” he explained. “I had to go through all that … I grieve him because I don’t get to live my life being able to call him up and say, “Yauch, you wouldn’t believe this thing happened, but I have to tell you about this … But I can think about what he might be thinking, or what his relationship would be to this thing that I’m going through, or just me making this record and what he might say.”.

Advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling upcoming approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies. The year before, however, the iPhone 16e arrived in February instead.

With Apple shaking up its normal iPhone rollout schedule, it was anyone’s guess how soon the fresh models would debut. But a March launch makes sense and gives Apple a trio of new iPhones every six months—three unveiled in September, and another three in March.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • iOS 27.3 launches next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.
  • Apple is granting iPhone Duo owners one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.
  • Face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient new option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 launches next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.

Apple is granting iPhone Duo owners one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.

Face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient new option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it. Per Apple:.

Sources indicate that use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to promptly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

According to recent reports, if your iPhone Duo has gone unused for 45 minutes or more, face unlock won’t work and you’ll need to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. But for most users, that probably just means using Touch ID first thing in the morning, then relying on face unlock the rest of the day.

On a related note, you can also enable Attention Aware features in iOS 27.3. These are available whether you use the face unlock feature or not, but are limited to the outer display. Once enabled, they can automatically lower the volume of alarms and timers, keep the display from dimming, and more.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds newly introduced face unlock feature for iPhone Duo.

It has been revealed that reachability is available on other iPhone models to move onscreen content down vertically, closer to your thumb. But on iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, Apple has a unique twist on the feature.

Instead of helping you reach content vertically, Reachability on iPhone Duo works horizontally.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

You can always disable Reachability if you find yourself accidentally triggering it too often. But if one-handed iPhone Duo use gives you trouble, Reachability is a great latest option to have.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bowen Yang has issued an apology for calling Regina Spektor an antisemitic slur on his “Las Culturistas” podcast, saying he was unaware of the word’s origins.

In a recent development, “I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we’ve repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks,” Yang wrote in an Instagram statement Friday. “Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against.”.

“At the same time, Free Palestine,” the comedian added in a follow-up Instagram Story.

It has been revealed that yang drew backlash this week when a clip of an October episode of his podcast with Matt Rogers began circulating on social media. Featuring guest, actress and comedian Edy Modica, the conversation turned to Spektor, and the trio wondered what the “Samson” singer has been up to since the release of her 2022 album Home, Before and After.

According to recent reports, modica remarked that Spektor had been “just, like, a little Israel hardcore,” referring to Spektor’s vocal pro-Israel advocacy. Yang added, “yeah, she’s Zio.”.

Short for Zionist, the derogatory term was popularized by Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke in the early 2000s and has been picked up by white supremacist groups.

The Anti-Defamation League recognizes the word as a hostile phrase when referring to Jewish people or Israelis. In response to Yang’s apology, Jonathan Greenblatt, the ADL’s CEO and National Director, slammed the comedian, saying it was “a textbook example of normalizing antisemitism.” Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Some Gamers Are Pissed That ‘GTA VI’ Makes Them Be Nice to Their Girlfriend Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi.

“Apologizing for your antisemitism with not one, but two qualifications isn’t an apology at all,” Greenblatt wrote in part.

According to recent reports, this post was updated on Friday, Nov. 20 at 4:30 p.m. to include a statement from the ADL’s Jonathan Greenblatt.

Bowers & Wilkins has long been one of our favorite brands for bookshelf speakers and headphones, but the name typically carries a high price tag. Their headphones fetch for $800, while the most high-end pair of B&W loudspeakers will set you back over $100,000.

In a recent development, fortunately, not every B&W product is that expensive — right now, the brand’s Px7 S2e over-ear noise-cancelling headphones are discounted to $229. Typically $400, the headphones feature a similar design to the brand’s most high-end models and identical battery life.

$229.00 $399.00 43% off.

Available in cloud grey, forest green, and ruby red.

It’s considerably less than the latest headphones from brands like Apple, Bose, and Sony, although certain colors are already sold out. For now, you can still pick up a pair of the headphones in cloud grey, forest green, and ruby red.

While we haven’t tested the Px7 S2e model, on paper, they have a lot of the same features that we love about the Px8 S2. They have the same solid 30-hour battery life, plus noise-canceling with an ambient setting. You also get wear detection (so the headphones pause when you take them off) and a zippered carrying case.

Sources indicate that the headphones also feature tactile buttons, rather than touch controls. There’s a slider to power the headphones on, distinct buttons for raising and lowering volume, a multifunction playback button, and a button to switch noise-canceling modes.

There are some tradeoffs with these headphones compared to the flagship model. B&W swapped the high-end leather finish for fabric, and the headphones use 40 mm bio-cellulose drivers, rather than the carbon drivers used by the Px8 S2 headphones.

According to recent reports, the flagship model also uses Qualcomm’s AptX Lossless codec for higher resolution audio over Bluetooth, compared to the AptX Adaptive codec used by the S2e model for high (although your source device has to support the codec for the best result). That mentioned, you still get many of the flagship model’s great features at a much (much) lower price.

$479.00 $749.00 36% off.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a higher-end pair of cans, Bowers & Wilkins’ first-gen Px8 headphones are also discounted. They feature the bells and whistles Bowers is known for, including Nappa leather earcups and aluminum details. The newer Px8 S2 features some upgrades, including a slimmer, more comfortable fit, but the Px8 are still top-tier headphones. It’s rare to find headphones made with leather and metal components at this price; for $479, they’re only slightly more expensive than other flagship headphones. Like Bowers’ other headphones, these feature up to 30 hours of battery life, which is enough for most trips and daily use.

#62671. Reverse Engineering my cat's litter box

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1473 w)

Reverse Engineering my cat's litter box

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1473 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Netlify

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maisie likes to touch the litter box while it is running.
  • My idea was to bring the litter box into Home Assistant, add some buttons, and eventually use presence sensors to start a cleaning cycle when she is in another room and distracted.
  • The phone app already knew how to do everything I needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maisie likes to touch the litter box while it is running. I would prefer that she find something else to do during that time.

My idea was to bring the litter box into Home Assistant, add some buttons, and eventually use presence sensors to start a cleaning cycle when she is in another room and distracted. There are probably many more automations I will come up with once I have that working. First, I needed a way to talk to the box.

The phone app already knew how to do everything I needed. I started by watching its traffic with Wireshark and inspecting HTTP requests with HTTP Toolkit, then decompiled the Android app to understand the parts I could not reproduce from the traffic alone.

This turned into two related projects. I needed to reproduce the signed HTTP requests used to access account and device data, then rebuild the binary messages used to operate the box over MQTT.

Industry observers note that the HTTP traffic exposed devices on the account, configuration, waste drawer levels, and records of litter box visits. I could also see how authentication worked. The app logs in to obtain a token, then includes that token in the Authorization header on later requests.

My first attempts to reproduce the requests returned 401 Unauthorized. Copying the endpoints and headers from a capture had not been enough. A 401 did not identify exactly which part of my reproduction was wrong, so I went back to comparing the app’s requests.

The X-UBT-Sign header kept changing. I could not work out its algorithm just by looking at the captured values. To generate my own requests, I needed to see how the app created it.

I used JADX to decompile the Android APK, then searched the recovered source for the header name and familiar backend strings:.

It has been revealed that the header name gave me a useful place to start in the decompiled code. It appears in sources/com/ubtrobot/infrastructure/a0.java, an obfuscated class whose retained metadata identifies it as UrcsSignInterceptor from HttpInterceptors.kt. The interceptor builds the signature and attaches it to outgoing HTTP requests. Its hashing helper, a.b.t, calls MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5").

The decompiled code demonstrates the final header being assembled and added to the request.

From sources/com/ubtrobot/infrastructure/a0.java:.

Industry observers note that the key is used for request signing. The Python implementation concatenates a timestamp in milliseconds, the app key, a nonce, and a client device ID, then calculates an MD5 digest:.

The order and formatting matter because the server needs to reproduce the same value. This is also why copying a single captured header would only get me so far. My client needed to generate a fresh signature for each request.

Finding the algorithm still left the application settings to sort out. During implementation, a mismatched client configuration produced an “illegal client” response. I followed the app’s regional bootstrap flow. In CountryViewModel, it configures a bootstrap server using an app ID and key embedded in the APK. The interface in sources/jb/a.java declares a request to /catbox-server/app/areaMap.

It has been revealed that that request is signed too. The embedded bootstrap key signs the region-discovery request, whose response supplies the regional app ID, app key, and API URL. The regional key then signs login and normal API requests. Following that chain let me obtain the matching US settings for my client.

From sources/com/ubtrobot/airpet/account/area/CountryViewModel.java:.

There were a few similarly named fields to keep straight:.

The login request separately hashes the account password with MD5. Its response includes token.token, the value to send in Authorization, and token.expireAt, the expiration time in milliseconds. I wrapped this in a small asynchronous HTTP client that reuses the token, logs in again shortly before expiration, and retries once after a 401.

The token structure is visible in my captured successful login response. I’ve redacted the credentials and omitted the account details.

From furrytail_login_response.json:.

Sources indicate that with that in place, I could turn the vendor’s responses into useful API endpoints like /device/waste and /device/summary. That gave me the data for a dashboard. Making a cleaning button required another layer of work.

The next clue came from something I did not see in Wireshark. When I pressed Clean in the app, there was no new HTTP request corresponding to the action.

Industry observers note that for a moment, I wondered whether the app was talking to the box over Bluetooth. But I could also operate the box remotely, so Bluetooth would not explain the whole command path.

Looking more closely at the app’s startup requests, I found /v1/ubtechinc-im-manager/im/login. Its response included mqttUserName, mqttPassword, clientId, pubTopic, and subTopic. That gave me another protocol to investigate, plus the credentials and topics needed to connect.

From sources/com/ubtrobot/urcs/connection/MqttInfoBean.java:.

The HTTP API supplies the MQTT session credentials, and a contacts endpoint helps identify the device’s messaging user ID.

In a recent development, I needed to keep track of both the client sending the message and the litter box receiving it. The serial number used by the HTTP endpoints is not the destination field used by the messaging protocol.

Sources indicate that my wrapper fetches the MQTT credentials at runtime and uses the device’s messaging ID to address commands. Now I had somewhere to send a message. I still needed to work out what that message should contain.

At the center of a cleaning command is a small Protocol Buffers message:.

Recent findings suggest that for a request to start cleaning, both values are 1. Serialized, the payload is just four bytes:.

Unfortunately, publishing those four bytes is not enough. The device expects a series of wrappers around them:.

There is quite a lot of packaging involved in asking a litter box to rotate.

It has been revealed that the RISP frame starts with a magic byte, 0xDB, followed by the length of a serialized header. That header includes the device category, command number, payload length, request attribute, and sequence number. An operation request uses command 1019.

Recent findings suggest that the frame also includes separate CRC-8 checksums for the header and payload. The implementation uses polynomial 0x07 with a final XOR of 0x55. These details are small, but they are part of the format the receiver expects.

The frame goes inside a protobuf Command. The serialized command is then wrapped in BytesValue, packed into Any, and placed in a custom instant-messaging message. That outer message carries the sender, recipient, message identifiers, timestamp, and protocol version.

The Any wrapper took some care. The outgoing message contains a BytesValue holding serialized command bytes. Packing the command directly into Any would produce a different message. Knowing the innermost schema only solves part of the problem.

Decompiled code helped explain the structure, but I also wanted visibility into the bytes the app was building.

I added a Frida script to inspect several points in the serialization path. It hooks the operation request, the RISP converter, the command’s toByteArray, and the outer messaging object’s toByteArray. Each hook logs the bytes at that layer and returns the original result.

This makes the nesting much easier to inspect. Instead of trying to understand one large binary payload all at once, I can look at the operation bytes separately from the command wrapper and the final MQTT message.

The decoder works back through the same layers, exposing the RISP header and known payload types. State responses include the work mode, work state, and sensor fields, which are much more useful for debugging than an unexplained byte array.

Once the message construction was in place, I could expose the operation through a normal HTTP endpoint:.

The wrapper handles the MQTT login, builds the nested message, and publishes it. The recreated command successfully operated the physical box, which was a satisfying result after working through all those layers.

The API also supports clear and smooth operations, plus start, pause, resume, and stop states. Home Assistant buttons can call these endpoints without needing to know anything about protobufs or checksums.

It has been revealed that for the data side, I added a script that pushes values into Home Assistant entities. It combines HTTP data, such as waste drawer percentage and visit history, with decoded MQTT state fields. This gives me a starting point for displaying the box’s status alongside the rest of the house.

There is still a dependency on the vendor’s cloud. The service runs locally, but it uses the vendor’s HTTP API and MQTT broker to communicate with the box. What I have now is a bridge that lets my own tools use those interfaces.

Sources indicate that next, I want to add presence sensors and figure out when Maisie is occupied elsewhere. That was the idea that started this project. Getting a button to operate the box was the first milestone. Deciding when to press it should give me plenty more things to work on.

Latest Update: GTA 6’s 30 FPS lock broke my PC gamer brain — until I turned on the one TV setting I swore I’d never touch

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve ever bought a new TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.
  • For movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder.
  • And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever bought a new TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.

For movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder. I hate it. Tom Cruise hates it. You should hate it too.

And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.

To understand how I ended up committing TV heresy, you have to understand the shock to the system that is GTA 6’s frame rate. Coming straight from my monster PC rig playing games like Resident Evil Requiem at up to 214 FPS, dropping back down to a strict 30 FPS console lock feels like wading through treacle.

It has been revealed that but on top of that, as I’ve seen (and you’ve seen on Digital Foundry’s test), that 30 FPS lock isn’t an actual lock. It can dip into the mid-20s during heavy scenes. Coming from super fluidity, that 30 FPS is brutal to adapt to.

So out of sheer desperation (and because we’re stuck waiting for the PC port), I broke the golden rule and toggled my TV’s smooth motion setting on.

And I hate to admit it, but it’s basically bootleg DLSS Frame Generation for your living room.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Just like PC frame generation tricks of old, your TV’s motion interpolation processor looks at two real frames from your console, guesses what should happen in between them, and inserts an artificial frame to smooth out the motion.

Sources indicate that the moment I flipped it on in GTA 6, that nauseating camera stutter when cruising down Ocean Beach vanished. Panning around a crowded street or taking a high-speed corner suddenly felt dramatically more fluid — nowhere near 60 fps, and definitely not my desktop rig, but miles smoother than the choppy presentation.

Sources indicate that before the AV forums come for my head with pitchforks, let’s be completely honest about the trade-offs. There is no such thing as a free lunch in frame interpolation:.

Because your TV has to wait for the next frame before it can invent the one in the middle, motion smooth adds latency between pressing a button and seeing the result on screen. In twitchy, competitive games, that’s a death sentence.

But in a Rockstar open-world game — where character movement is already famously weighty and deliberate — I never noticed that extra latency.

Industry observers note that your TV’s processor is just guessing after all, and while it is a good guesser, there are some moments of weird shimmering around fast-moving objects and some boiling around on-screen elements like subtitles. Probably compounded by the fact GTA 6 is already running its own resolution scaling tech under the hood.

It has been revealed that standard Game Mode and VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) automatically lock out motion smoothing on many TVs. Depending on your set, you either have to turn on the dedicated low-latency Game Motion Plus mode (found on newer Samsung and LG sets) or sacrifice VRR to unlock it.

The silver lining, though, is that with this being a 30 FPS game, it’s not high enough to require VRR anyway.

If GTA 6’s 30 FPS cap is giving your eyes a workout and you want to test the dark arts yourself, don’t just blindly max out every slider.

If your TV has a low-latency interpolation option (like Samsung’s Game Motion Plus or LG’s TruMotion tweaks), use that before turning off Game Mode completely.

Industry observers note that set Judder Reduction to a middle ground (around 5-7 out of 10) rather than maxing it out. You want to take the harsh edge off camera pans without turning your car into a blurry smudge.

This is optional based on personal taste. Test how your TV’s smoothing looks with GTA’s built-in motion blur turned off. For a lot of OLED owners, letting the TV handle the smoothing cleanly beats stacking two different blur effects on top of each other.

Do I want to play GTA 6 at native 240 FPS on my PC rig? Obviously. The second Rockstar drops the PC version, I’ll be uninstalling this hack from my brain and never looking back.

Industry observers note that I still wouldn’t be caught dead watching a movie with motion smoothing turned on. But until PC gamers get their turn in Vice City, breaking the ultimate TV rule is the best survival trick I’ve found for making a 30 FPS masterpiece actually feel better to play.

According to recent reports, also yes, my wife has taken note of the fact that I share the same name as the male protagonist. And yes, she is side-eyeing how I treat Lucia hard.

According to recent reports, amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Industry observers note that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a latest model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

In a recent development, if you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

According to recent reports, if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

Sources indicate that if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's at the moment pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

It has been revealed that if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, right now marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (at the moment $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

In a recent development, follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chromebooks are distributed to students through a fence at a Los Angeles Unified School District high school for during the Covid quarantine.
  • Hundreds of workers at Google are pushing senior leadership to retract a policy that would block schools who turn off its Gemini AI tools from access to the firm’s search engine starting next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chromebooks are distributed to students through a fence at a Los Angeles Unified School District high school for during the Covid quarantine. Sarah Reingewirtz/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News/Getty.

Hundreds of workers at Google are pushing senior leadership to retract a policy that would block schools who turn off its Gemini AI tools from access to the firm’s search engine starting next year.

Sources indicate that google made the surprise announcement two weeks ago, on Election Day, with executives saying they wanted to address teachers and parents’ concerns around AI in the classroom. Since then, communities across the country have protested Google’s tight hold on tech in many schools.

As I wrote last week after attending a rally in Latest York City:.

Attendees of all ages held signs reading, “NO AI IN MY SCHOOL!”, “A.I. Gets an F,” “Stop stealing our imaginations,” and “SCHOOL Librarians = THE BEST Search Engines.” Some students handed out fliers to passersby while younger children ran around and drew pictures off to the side.

Many cars driving by honked their horns in support, and a few construction workers on the other side of the one-way street cheered the protesters on.

That day, protests took place in six other cities—Los Angeles; Chicago; Boston; Portland, Oregon; Boulder, Colorado; and Durham, North Carolina—all organized by a nationwide alliance of parent and community advocacy organizations.

School districts across the country use the firm’s software and Chromebooks, which were more affordable than Windows and Apple computers when many were promptly assembling remote learning programs during the early years of the Covid pandemic. The Chromebooks have built-in AI classroom tools, and Google Search embeds AI Overview and AI Mode powered by Gemini.

Responding to the backlash, three of the largest school districts in the US—Fresh York City, Los Angeles, and Chicago—are now discussing alternative search engines.

“Any opportunity to drive positive change with AI in education will rely on educators having the freedom to choose how to implement it in their curriculum,” employees wrote in a petition brought by the Alphabet Workers Union, which represents more than 1,000 workers at Google’s parent company. “Cutting off access to Search for schools that don’t wish to use AI will not help persuade our users, and will more likely result in them shutting out Google products altogether.”.

“It is our job as Googlers to respect the user, and listen to them when they have concerns about our products,” they continued, addressing Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Google vice president and general manager of education Chris Phillips, and Elizabeth Reid, its vice president and head of search.

A software engineer in Google’s education department told me on Thursday that most workers did not know about the Google Search decision before it was publicly unveiled. Corporate leadership has now acknowledged the letter but has not responded to any of its specific demands.

AI classroom tools should be “built responsibly and prioritize the best interests of the students, not the manufacturer’s bottom line,” the Google engineer noted.

Another engineer and union member in Newly introduced York, who also signed the petition, mentioned to Mother Jones that the executive team “seems convinced that resistance to AI adoption is because people don’t see the vision.”.

That goes beyond teachers, parents, and students: the Google staffer said their colleagues are also concerned about how the manufacturer is implementing their work on AI tools.

“If the tech is really as useful and desirable as they think it is, why don’t they trust us to choose to use it on our own terms?” the engineer asked.

Google has been contacted for comment.

Amid accusations of antisemitism over a recent episode of Las Culturistas, Bowen Yang has issued an apology.

On Friday, the 5x Emmy nominee released a statement explaining he was unaware of the “antisemitic history” of the word “Zio,” which he recently used in reference to Regina Spektor removing a pro-Palestine protester from her concert.

“I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we’ve repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks,” he wrote in the statement on Instagram. “Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against.”.

Yang added on his Instagram Story, “At the same time, Free Palestine.” Watch on Deadline.

Although some thought Yang’s apology wasn’t enough, many in the comments have called out the criticism for being in bad faith, with the common assumption that the term is short for “Zionism,” which originated in the 19th century as a movement to establish a Jewish homeland.

But the ADL considers it to be an “antisemitic slur popularized by notorious white supremacist leader and former KKK Grand Wizard David Duke,” with ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt accusing Yang of providing “a textbook example of normalizing antisemitism.”.

“Seriously? Apologizing for your antisemitism with not one, but two qualifications isn’t an apology at all,” wrote Greenblatt in part. “It was a reminder that you don’t feel like Jews deserve the same respect as everyone else. That’s not political speech; it’s prejudice — and it’s pathetic.”.

Despite accusations of antisemitism, Yang and Las Culturistas co-host Matt Rogers have called out Zionism on multiple occasions as it pertains to the occupation of Gaza.

It has been revealed that since Israel’s ongoing strikes on Gaza in the wake of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack, multiple organizations have classified Israel’s actions as a genocide against Palestinians, including the United Nations, Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch.
